AdvanceSceneDataAndFree:
Skip a defeated enemy during scene actor spawning and return its slot to the pool.

Called from InitActorFromSceneData when CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag returns carry set (enemy already permanently killed). Y holds the stream offset into the current actor record.

Two outcomes based on whether more actors remain:

1. More actors follow (next byte ≠ $FF): Advances the scene data pointer $3E past the remaining record bytes (Y + 1 + $3E → $3E). Branches directly to InitActorFromSceneData to process the next actor record in the same spawn loop iteration.

2. End of actor list (next byte = $FF): Returns the allocated slot to the actor free list by decrementing $4E twice (backing up the free list pointer by one word) and writing the slot address (TXA) via STA [$4E]. Decrements activeActorCount ($0DBC). Unlinks the slot from the actor chain by zeroing the previous actor's next pointer ($0006,Y = 0). Sets X to the previous actor (TYX) and returns with carry set to signal SpawnSceneActors that this actor was skipped.
AdvanceTileOffsetX:
Advance the tile map offset one tile RIGHT (+X).

Increments the low nibble of $00 — the next column inside the 16×16 page. If the low nibble wraps to zero, the page's right edge was crossed: the carry has bumped the row nibble, so +$F0 undoes it, and the high byte is incremented (next page column). Result in Y. Same operation as map_coords.MapIndexMoveRight.
AdvanceTileOffsetY:
Advance the tile map offset one tile DOWN (+Y).

Adds $10 to the low byte of $00 — the next row inside the 16×16 page. If the addition carries (crossed the page's bottom edge), adds mapRowStrideL0 to the high byte to reach the same column of the next page row. Result in Y. Same operation as map_coords.MapIndexMoveDown.
ApplyHitDamageToVictim:
Resolve one phase-2 overlap: apply player-strength damage to the overlapped actor (X = victim, $08 = box owner / hitter). It reduces the victim actor's HP; contact damage to the player is ApplyInteractionDamage.

Two main paths based on $24 flag (set by the friendly/interaction detection in the outer loop):

Path 1 ($24 nonzero — interaction/push hit): Checks the enemy's scratch1010+6 ($7F1016,X) for a custom interaction handler. If present, overwrites the enemy's entry point. Otherwise, sets the enemy to SpawnImpactSparkAndDie (player_transition_handlers), marks $0040 (death flag), and dispatches knockback velocity by player facing direction (±4 to extVelocityX/Y).

Path 2 ($24 zero — combat damage, the code under ApplyHitDamageToVictim_DamagePath): Checks if the victim has $0010 in flags10 (invincible) → routes to HitInvincibleVictim. Otherwise computes damage:
  totalStr = playerStr + rangedDamageBonus ($09E2, 0 for hitter slot $1000) + abilityDamageBonus ($09E0)
  rawDamage = max(1, totalStr − victimStats[2])   (stats[2] = DEF)
  netDamage = rawDamage + characterForm
Subtracts from enemy HP, spawns damage digits (spawn flags $2B00, then $12 bit $1000 of the spawned actor is set: the display-filter qualifier that lets it run in RunActors_DisplayFiltered), handles death (onDeathCallback or StandardEnemyDefeatHandler), and spawns HitStaggerMain for knockback.

After damage: checks and dispatches onHitCallback ($7F1000,X). Assigns iframeCounter: $FFEF (negative = recovery: counts up toward zero, the tick still runs) when $12 bit 0 ($0001) is set, otherwise $0011 (positive = hit-stun: non-player actors skip their tick, the player's tick still runs). Updates HUD HP display. Finally checks extendedFlags $0050 for collision callback processing — clears $FFAF bits, toggles $6000 in $12, and dispatches onCollideCallback.
ApplyHitDamageToVictim_DamagePath:
Second half of ApplyHitDamageToVictim. Its first two instructions (TXY, RTS) are the landing pad of the PEA label−1 RTS trick that finishes the push/knockback path of the handler (Y = X on return). The rest of the part, entered at loc_03BF86 when $24 is zero, is the combat-damage path: totalStr = playerStr + rangedDamageBonus + abilityDamageBonus, rawDamage = max(1, totalStr − victim DEF), netDamage = rawDamage + characterForm, victim HP clamped at 0.

Then it spawns the damage digits (skipped for $12 bit 5 bosses), marks the victim $0080, resolves death inline (onDeathCallback or StandardEnemyDefeatHandler) or spawns HitStaggerMain, dispatches and clears onHitCallback, sets iframeCounter ($FFEF = negative = recovery when $12 bit 0 ($0001) is set, otherwise $0011 = positive = hit-stun: non-player actors skip their tick, the player's tick still runs), plays hit sound #05, updates the HUD HP registers and finally handles the onCollideCallback of the attacker. A player with the invincible flag ($10 bit 4) is diverted to HitInvincibleVictim.
ApplyInteractionDamage:
Apply damage or interaction effect when player contacts an actor.

If the target has $0020 flag (NPC/friendly), routes to InteractionDamage_NPCChat for dialogue handling.

For combat actors: computes the interaction hitbox center (with H-mirror), loads enemy attack power from stats table offset 1. Damage = max(1, enemyAtk − playerDef). Subtracts from playerHp (clamped to 0). Sets the $0080 (iframe) flag and assigns iframeCounter $003C (60; positive = hit-stun: non-player actors skip their tick, the player's tick still runs), longer than the $0011 that combat assigns.

If playerFlags bits 11|12 ($1800) are clear (no script/ability lock and not on a slope): spawns HitStaggerMain (spawn flags $2400), copies extendedFlags $0020 to the stagger actor, masks joypad ($0F00), computes knockback direction via CalcKnockbackFromActorCenters.

Plays character-form-specific hit sound: Freedan/Shadow = #08, Will = #07.
ApplyMovement:
Simple movement delta application without collision checking.

Reads X delta from override chain pointer $2C (if set) or moveScratch1 ($7F002C,X). If direction flag $12 bit 14 ($4000) is set, negates the delta (X flip). Adds result to actor X position $14 and clears moveScratch1.

Y axis is identical: reads from $2E / moveScratch2, negates per $12 bit 13 ($2000), applies to $16.

Override pointers form a linked chain: $0000,Y = movement value, $0002,Y = next link pointer (written to $2C/$2E for the next frame). If the pointer is zero, falls through to the per-actor scratch field.

Called by the actor post-tick when bit 3 ($0008) of $10 is clear, and by RunActors_OverlayOnly for every overlay actor.
ApplyMovementWithCollision:
Collision-aware movement entry point — axis-separated tile collision pipeline.

Pre-computes the lower Y camera bound (absolute scratch $0004 = cameraLowerYBound − $0010) for vertical clipping; MoveUp/MoveDown compare against it. Then processes X and Y axes independently:

X axis: reads delta from override $2C or moveScratch1, negates per $12 bit 14. PEA pushes CollisionX_PostMove − 1 as the return address, then dispatches to TileCollision_MoveLeft (negative delta) or TileCollision_MoveRight (positive). The collision routine returns via RTS into CollisionX_PostMove.

Y axis: same pattern with $2E / moveScratch2, bit 13, dispatching to MoveUp/MoveDown via CollisionY_Setup.

Called by the actor post-tick when bit 3 ($0008) of $10 is set.
ApplyScrollWaveEffect:
Apply one frame of sine-wave scroll distortion via HDMA.

Calls ComputeSineScrollTable to fill two identical back-to-back 256-word scroll-offset tables, sineTableA ($7E8900) and sineTableB ($7E8B00). Then builds a two-segment indirect HDMA table at $7E8800 whose window starts at word (($36 & $01FE) / 2) of that doubled table, so the wave moves with the NMI frame counter $36:
- $7E8800: $FF — HDMA line-count byte (bit 7 = repeat mode, bits 0–6 = 127 scanlines)
- $7E8801: data pointer = $8900 + ($36 & $01FE)
- $7E8803: $E0 — repeat mode, 96 scanlines
- $7E8804: data pointer = first pointer + $FE (127 words on, so the window continues without a gap)
- $7E8806: $00 (end marker)

Because the second table copy directly follows the first, a window starting anywhere in the first 256 words never wraps (223 scanlines in total). Queues HDMA channels 6 and 7 via COP [QueueHdmaChannel] with B-bus registers $0D (BG1HOFS, $210D) and $0F (BG2HOFS, $210F) and indirect data bank $7E, both reading the same table. Then calls UpdateFrameDialogue for one frame of display sync.
ArrivalAndTravelSetup: Child actor (flags $3800, script-driven). Phases: a zoom-out of 44 passes at 2 ticks per pass (about 88 ticks; $B8 falls), for a menu trip a 16-tick wait + WorldMapSplitEffect + wait for the player's route, the 93-tick tilt phase with the start name ($B6 grows), then the companion dots. It finally becomes the leader's dot through the shared loop in CompanionDotMovement and dies when the route ends.
BuildSplitTables: Rebuild both HDMA tables for the buffer chosen by frame parity (Y = $0000 even, $0100 odd, with DBR = $7E): copy template 1 into $8800,Y and template 2 into $8A00,Y, adding the actor's offset ($7F2104,X) to each template's second line count (byte 2), and write the $0000 terminator after the BGMODE table only. The COLDATA table has no terminator; its tail is the fill from InitSplitFill.
BuildSplitTablesCopy: Copy both templates into the selected buffer pair.
CalcKnockbackDirection:
Compute knockback direction from attacking and defending actor hitbox centers.

Loads the attacking actor from $0BFE,Y (render list back-reference). If the attacker IS the player, returns with carry set (caller should use GetPlayerFacing instead).

Otherwise computes the attacker's hitbox center: reads metasprite hitbox offsets ($0004–$0007), sign-extends, halves the width/height (LSR), and adds to position. Accounts for H-mirror via carry flag.

Computes the defender's center: reads hitbox fields ($20–$23), halves, and adds to position.

Then determines direction by comparing axis deltas: |centerX_attacker − centerX_defender| vs |centerY_attacker − centerY_defender|. Returns: 0=south (defender below), 1=north (defender above), 2=west (defender left), 3=east (defender right). Returns carry clear to signal a valid direction.
CalcKnockbackFromActorCenters:
Compute knockback direction from raw actor center positions (not hitbox centers).

Simpler version of CalcKnockbackDirection: uses actor positions with ±4px adjustment instead of metasprite hitbox center calculation. Compares axis deltas to determine cardinal direction (0=S, 1=N, 2=W, 3=E).

Returns direction in A. Used by ApplyInteractionDamage for interaction knockback where precise hitbox geometry is not needed.
CalcTileMapOffset:
Convert tile coordinates ($18 = X, $1C = Y) to a tile map byte offset in Y.

The map is stored as 256-byte pages of 16×16 tiles. The offset's low byte is (tileY & $F) << 4 | (tileX & $F) (row-major inside the page); its high byte is the page number = (tileY >> 4) × mapRowStrideL0 + (tileX >> 4), where the product comes from hardware Multiply8x8Unsigned (A low byte = stride, B = tileY >> 4 left over from the shift). Returns the 16-bit offset in Y.

The tile map is accessed via long pointer [$80] which points to the current scene's collision data.
CheckActorOnSpecialTile:
Check if the actor is standing on special tile patterns that bypass normal collision.

Saves $18/$1C. Probes the tile at (actorX − 8, actorY − 16) — the tile above-left of the actor origin. If either coordinate is tile-aligned (low 4 bits = 0), returns CLC (no special tile).

Converts to tile coordinates and reads the collision map. Two detection patterns:

1. Tile = $06: checks the (+X,+Y) diagonal neighbor. If that is also $06, returns SEC (special).
2. Tile = $00 (empty): checks the tile to the right (+X); if it is $09, restores the offset and checks the tile below (+Y). If both are $09, returns SEC (L-shaped special pattern).

All other tiles or incomplete patterns → CLC (normal collision applies). Callers treat SEC as "axis blocked" (see header).
CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag:
Check if an enemy was already defeated, via its enemy-defeat flag bit (wramFlags at $0A80; set by SetDungeonKillFlag/SetWramFlag when the enemy dies). The flags persist until ClearAllWramFlags runs (world map entry, st68_kara, sp58_red_eye) or game over clears them; no reset at ordinary scene changes was found in extracted/ (see flag_helpers).

Converts enemy number A to a byte index (÷8 → Y) and bit position (AND #$07 → X). Looks up a bitmask from BitMaskTable_Wram ($01/$02/$04/$08/$10/$20/$40/$80) and ANDs it with the WRAM flag byte at $0A80,Y.

If the bit is set (enemy defeated): checks for an associated event block swap. Reads the event block index (record byte 8) from the scene data at the saved Y offset. If nonzero, calls event_blocks.LookupEventBlock and event_blocks.CopyEventBlockTiles to update the tilemap for the defeated enemy's area (e.g., removing a barrier or revealing a passage). Returns carry set.

If the bit is clear (enemy alive): returns carry clear.
CheckInventoryForItem:
Check if an item exists in the player's inventory.

Searches all 16 inventorySlots for the item ID in A. Returns carry clear if found, carry set if not found.
CheckPlayerDeath:
Check if the player has died and trigger game over sequence.

Guards: returns immediately if playerFlags bit 5 ($0020) is set (boss-defeat latch) or bit 9 ($0200) is set (game over sequence active). If playerHp ($0ACE) is zero and neither guard is set, sets $0200 in playerFlags, overwrites the player actor's entry point to GameOverSequence, and calls StopPlayerOnDeath to halt all movement.
CheckPlayerSpriteCache:
Check whether the player's sprite data needs VRAM re-upload.

Compares the current metasprite pointer ($7F000C,X) and sprite bank ($7F0008,X) against cached values at $09CC and $09CE. If both match and the force-redraw flag (bit 2 $0004 in playerFlags) is not set, returns the cached pointer — no VRAM update needed.

On cache miss: clears the force-redraw flag, stores the new pointer and bank to $09CC/$09CE, and sets bit 3 ($0008) in displayModeFlags to trigger a player tile DMA during the next VBlank.
CheckSceneTransition:
Quick test for pending scene transitions.

Checks two trigger sources:
1. Staged world-map entry $0D52/$0D53 (the destination X word written by the world-map COP handlers; nonzero = pending)
2. sceneNext ($0642, nonzero = normal scene change pending)

If either is nonzero, falls through to ExecuteSceneTransition. Otherwise returns immediately via RTL. Called every frame from the main game loop.
ClearActorRenderList:
Clear the depth-sort bucket array at $0200 in preparation for the next frame.

Zeroes 512 bytes ($0200–$03FE, 256 words) and writes $FFFF as an end sentinel at $0400. This array is used by SortActorsByDepth as bucket storage for the Y-position depth sort. Called only at scene setup (scene_lifecycle) and by inventory_overlay; during normal frames the sort leaves the buckets zeroed on its own.
ClearSaveSlot:
Zero an entire SRAM save slot.

Slot number in A (masked to 0–3). Fills $0100 words (512 bytes) at $306200 + slot offset with zero. This erases both the event flag data and the checksums, making the slot appear empty to LoadGameState_Scene.

Returns with carry set (convention — matches the load failure return).
ClearSceneState:
Comprehensive scene state reset and initialization — the 'big setup' function.

Called by ExecuteSceneTransition after resolving the target scene. Performs a complete teardown and rebuild of the game world in a fixed sequence:

=== PHASE 1: CLEAR STATE ===
Disables HDMA. Zeroes all critical game variables: joypad masks, cached HP, display mode, player flags, the first event-flag word ($0A00 = flags $00–$0F only), camera targets/deltas, scroll positions/overrides, player speeds, external velocities, enemy health timer, climb state, actor count, DMA skip flag. Sets invincibility timer to $FFFF (disabled). Clears backdrop colors and COLDATA. Resets BG3 tilemap base ($78 = VRAM $7800), the BG1/BG2 character base ($22), MOSAIC, and all window mask/logic registers. Clears event flag $FF (bit 7 of the $0A1F flag byte), which phase 3 sets again.

=== PHASE 2: LOAD SCENE ===
Calls subsystems in order:
1. ClearBg3TilemapBuffer_Full — zero the BG3 staging buffer
2. SceneScriptMain — parse scene script (loads tileset, tilemap, music, display config)
3. InitCameraBounds — set camera limits from map bounds or custom $0652 data
4. ApplyAllEventBlocks — apply persistent event-driven tile changes
5. PlaceOpenedChestTiles — write the open-chest tiles of every chest whose event flag is set (records of scene_chest_table) to the map
6. InitActorPool — reset actor/thinker pools
7. SpawnSceneActors — instantiate actors from scene definition table
8. DisplaySceneTitle — display centered area name overlay if entering a new scene
9. SpawnSceneThinkers — instantiate thinkers from scene definition table

=== PHASE 3: PREPARE RENDERING ===
10. LoadScenePalettes — load scene/character palettes
11. LoadPlayerGraphics — DMA player sprite tiles to VRAM
12. ClearActorRenderList — reset the OAM render list
13. InitWarpTable — set up warp zone collision rectangles
14. RunActors_Normal ×2 — run two frames of actor AI to settle initial positions
15. ResetHdmaState ×2 — clear HDMA channels (once before thinkers, once after)
16. RunThinkers_General/B — execute both thinker phases
17. Set $FF sentinel in OAM buffer, sort actors, compose sprites
18. DmaPlayerTilesToVram — initial player tile upload

=== PHASE 4: RENDER TILEMAP ===
Two paths based on scrollModeFlags bit 3:
- Set: Calls RenderPaletteTiles (palette-based scene, no scrolling BG)
- Clear: Calls CameraFullRefresh for layer 0 (if $069B nonzero) and layer 1 (if $069D nonzero) to render the full visible tilemap

Finally clears musicRoomGroup, effect deltas, and related scroll variables.
ClearStateLoop: Zero-fill loop of ClearWorldMapState: 14 words from $0D52 to $0D6D.
CollisionX_PostMove:
Post-collision handler for the X axis — applies residual movement after tile check.

Returned to via PEA/RTS from MoveLeft/MoveRight. Carry flag from the collision routine indicates result: set = blocked, clear = passed.

If not blocked (carry clear), reads residual delta from override chain or moveScratch1 (same negation logic as the initial path) and adds to $14. Clears moveScratch1 regardless.

Then begins the Y axis pipeline: reads Y delta from $2E / moveScratch2, stores to $001E, negates per $12 bit 13, and dispatches to MoveUp/MoveDown with CollisionY_Setup as the PEA return.
CollisionY_Setup:
Post-collision handler for the Y axis, plus bounce/reflect detection.

Same residual-movement pattern as CollisionX_PostMove but for Y: applies remaining Y delta to $16 if not blocked. Clears moveScratch2.

After movement, checks for the bounce condition:
1. $10 bit 2 ($0004) = solid contact occurred this frame
2. extendedFlags bit 6 ($0040) = bounce flag (set by actor AI scripts)

If both are set, clears the bounce flag and reverses both direction bits by EOR $6000 on $12 — effectively reflecting the actor's movement direction on both axes.
CombatCollision_EnemyLoop:
Main combat collision iteration loop — tests player attacks and enemy contact.

Two-phase collision detection per enemy:

Phase 1 (player attack test): For each actor Y in the render list, checks eligibility (actors without $0400 only): bit 7 ($0080) of $10 set (hit-reaction active), bit 6 ($0040) clear (not dead/orb), and $12 bit 4 ($0010) clear (not damage-immune). If eligible and the enemy's iframe counter is non-negative, calls PlayerAttackHitTest.

Phase 2 (enemy-hits-player test): After phase 1, constructs the current enemy's AABB from metasprite hitbox fields ($0004–$0007), accounting for H-mirror via the carry flag from ASL on $000E. Then iterates the render list again (inner loop at CombatCollision_InnerLoop), testing each actor's hitbox ($0020–$0023) for AABB overlap against the enemy's box.

The $20 DP flag distinguishes normal mode (exclusion mask $76E0) from friendly/interaction mode ($74E0 + extendedFlags $0010 check). On overlap, calls ApplyHitDamageToVictim.
CombatCollision_Exit: Common exit of the combat pipeline: PLB, PLP, RTL.
companion_formation_tables: Formation layouts indexed by the number of companions N (entry N; entry 6 is never reached because at most 5 companions are scanned). Each layout is a list of screen-offset pairs (X, Y) from the camera target, the first for the leader. N = 1 uses formation_leader_plus_1 (two dots side by side), N = 4 uses formation_leader_plus_4, all others use formation_leader_plus_5.
CompanionDotMovement:
A companion's dot. Entry: it was spawned at the leader's position, so it glides to its own formation slot (camera + slot pair) at 1 pixel per frame, then joins the shared dot loop at DotAnimationLoop.
Actor fields: $24 = own slot pair (low byte X, high byte Y, screen offsets), $26 = leader's slot pair (copied to orbitDiameter as home), $28 = animation index.
ComposeAllSprites:
Main per-frame sprite composition entry point — builds the complete OAM table.

Pre-fills all 128 OAM entries with the hidden value $E080 (X $80, Y $E0 = below the screen) by pushing $E080 × 256 words onto a temporary stack at $0621. Then processes two sprite sources:

1. RenderComposeBuffer: converts pre-composed sprites from $7F3100 to OAM entries
2. Sorted actor list ($0C00): for each actor, calls DecomposeActorMetasprites to expand metasprite definitions into individual OAM entries

OAM state: $06 points to the current hi-table byte (starts at $0622), $0E counts sprites left in the current hi-table group (4 per byte) and $00 is the rolling hi-table shift register. $08 is not OAM state: it is the write pointer of the player tile-DMA list (starts at $06FE), and $14 is the sequential OAM tile counter for player sub-sprites. After the compose buffer has been consumed, the compose-buffer write offset ($00D8) is reset so the next frame's entries start at $7F3100.

When the actor list is exhausted (zero entry) or OAM is full (carry set from decomposition), finalizes the hi-table remainder by shifting and storing the last partial byte.
ComposeDigitSprites:
Main entry point for damage digit composition.

Reads packed BCD from DP $0000. If any bit of $F000 is set (not a valid packed number) it returns without drawing; FormatDamageDigits cannot produce such a value, so this is only a defensive check. Otherwise it sets the cursor X to actorX − 12, Y to DP $16 and the attribute to DP $0E, then processes digits left-to-right: hundreds → tens → ones. Each digit that is not a leading zero is drawn via EmitDigitOamEntry (+8px); a leading zero is not drawn and advances the cursor by only 4px.
ComposeDigitSprites_AtCursor:
Second entry that skips the actor-position setup and the $F000 guard.

The caller supplies the digit X cursor ($0018), Y ($001C) and attribute ($0002) itself; the diary counter does this from the BG1 scroll position. The routine copies $0018 to $001A (not read anywhere in this file), moves the cursor left by 6px, and joins ComposeDigitSprites at its hundreds-digit step (loc_03BB0D). Purpose of the 6px shift: not documented (inferred as a fixed alignment offset for the diary counter, the only user).
ComputeSaveChecksum:
Compute dual checksums over SRAM save data for integrity verification.

Operates on $00FE words (254 entries = 508 bytes) starting at $306200,X where X is the pre-computed slot offset.

Two running accumulators, both seeded with $3652 (non-zero, so a zeroed slot does not match its stored zero checksums):
- $0018: additive checksum — sum of all data words
- $001C: XOR checksum — running XOR of all data words

Both are order-independent, so swapping two words is not detected. Uses DP $0018, $001C and $000E as scratch.
ComputeSineScrollTable:
Build per-scanline horizontal scroll offset tables for HDMA wave effect.

For each of 256 entries ($0200 bytes = 256 words per table):
1. Reads a signed sine value from sine_table_8bit, indexed by Y (starts at 0 and advances by the spatial frequency $0070 per entry). sine_table_8bit holds only the 64-entry first quarter, so Y ≥ 64 reads on into the adjacent signed_cosine_table_8bit; together they form a full 256-step signed sine cycle (see the math_lookup_tables block note)
2. Multiplies the sine value by the wave amplitude ($006E) using the SNES hardware multiplier ($4202/$4203 → $4216/$4217)
3. For negative sine values: performs sign-extended multiplication using $FF multiply + carry-based addition of the low byte
4. Adds the base BG1 horizontal scroll ($bg1ScrollH) to the offset
5. Stores the result to both sineTableA ($7E8900,X) and sineTableB ($7E8B00,X) — identical copies, so ApplyScrollWaveEffect can read a window that runs past the end of the first copy
6. Advances the sine index Y by the spatial frequency ($0070) per entry

If DP $00 is zero, returns immediately without filling the tables. Callers store a nonzero loop counter there (frame delay, brightness or ramp counter); the amplitude itself is $006E.

The index step $0070 sets the spatial frequency (6 gives six full sine cycles across the 256 entries); $006E scales the peak offset (about amplitude / 2 pixels, from the high byte of amplitude × sine). Together they produce the 'wavy screen' effect seen during scene transitions.
ConsoleCmd_ClearColumn:
Clear a variable-width column region downward through the VRAM buffer.

2-byte operand (text tag [CLR:pos], not used by any vanilla string): buffer offset of the top-left tile. First scans rightward from there, testing only the low byte of each tile word, counting words until one is zero; that count minus one is stored as the width. Then blanks width tiles plus the tile after them in each row (so the whole measured run), advancing down by $0040, and stops when the first tile of the next row is zero (word test). A run of one tile gives width 0, which makes the 16-bit counter wrap and clear 64K words, so it must not be used that way. The TAY after reading the trailing tile is dead (the result is never used).

Erases a text block whose width is read from the tiles already on screen. It does not move the cursor.
ConsoleCmd_ClearRect:
Clear a rectangular area of the VRAM staging buffer.

2-byte operand: byte 0 = width, byte 1 = height. Fills (width + 1) × (height + 1) tiles with $0000 (blank, attribute 0) starting at the current cursor position: the inner loop writes width+1 tiles (BPL loop from width down to 0), and the row loop runs until the height counter goes negative. Rows are $0040 bytes apart.

Hazard: the height counter is loaded as a 16-bit word, so the byte AFTER the operand becomes its high byte. This only works when that byte is $00, so every use in the game is the last command before the end byte (e.g. [POS:0,0][RCC:1F,4]). Any other following byte would make the loop run for hundreds of rows. It does not change the cursor on the stack.
ConsoleCmd_DoubleNewLine:
Line break of two tilemap rows (text tag [DBL]).

Adds $0080 (128 bytes = 2 rows × 32 words/row × 2 bytes/word) to the line start in $09A0 and writes the result to $09A0 and the saved X on the stack. Double the step of ConsoleCmd_NewLine.
ConsoleCmd_DrawBox:
Draw a bordered UI rectangle with corners, edges, and interior fill.

4-byte operand (text tag [BOX:w,h,pos]): 1-byte interior width + 1-byte interior height + 2-byte buffer offset of the top-left corner. Constructs the box using tile types OR'd with the $099E attribute word:
- $10: corner tiles (4 variants via V/H flip: $0010 TL, $4010 TR, $8010 BL, $C010 BR)
- $11: horizontal edges (top $0011, bottom $8011)
- $12: vertical edges (left $0012, right $4012)
- $40: interior fill

Draws top row (corner + edges + corner), then height rows of (border + fill + border), then bottom row. After drawing, the cursor and line start become box start + $0082 (2 rows down, 1 column right of the top-left corner, which is the second interior row, not the first).
ConsoleCmd_DrawEnemyHpBar:
Draw the enemy's HP bar using the same segment algorithm as player HP.

No operand. Uses enemyHpCurrentDisplay ($09E6) as current HP and enemyHpDisplay ($09E4) as the maximum. Same clamp (max above 40 is clamped in place, then HP) and segment calculation as ConsoleCmd_DrawPlayerHpBar. Sets the palette word to $0400 (palette 1) and calls DrawHpBar.
ConsoleCmd_DrawPlayerHpBar:
Draw the player's HP bar using filled, half, and empty segments.

No operand. If playerMaxHp ($0ACA) exceeds 40 ($28) it is clamped to 40 in RAM and playerHp ($0ACE) is then clamped the same way (HP is not checked when the maximum is already ≤ 40). Computes three segment counts in DP scratch:
- $00 = full segments (playerHp / 2)
- $08 = half-unit flag (1 if playerHp is odd)
- $02 = empty segments ((maxHP − HP) / 2, plus one when the three counts do not cover maxHP, i.e. an odd maximum)

Sets the palette word to $0800 (palette 2) in $04 and calls DrawHpBar with A = the cursor.
ConsoleCmd_End:
Terminate the Console string renderer and return to the caller.

Command $00 (the string terminator). Called via JSR from the main loop, so it first pops that call's return address (PLA) and the pushed X (PLX), then restores the data bank and processor status pushed at ConsoleStringRenderer's entry (PLB/PLP) and returns to the JSL caller with RTL. This is the only exit from the rendering loop.
ConsoleCmd_FillTile:
Fill N tile positions with a single tile value.

3-byte operand (text tag [CPY:tile,addr], not used by any vanilla string): 1-byte tile index + 2-byte address of a 16-bit repeat count (current data bank). The tile byte replaces the low byte of the $099E attribute word to form the tile word, which is written count times (nothing if the count is 0). The cursor is advanced past the run.
ConsoleCmd_IndirectString:
Render a string selected by an indirect index lookup.

5-byte operand (text tag [TBL:@table,addr]): 2-byte table address + 1-byte bank + 2-byte address of the index variable. Reads the 16-bit index from that address (in the caller's data bank, so a RAM variable), multiplies by 2, adds it to the table address, sets the data bank to the table's bank, reads the string pointer from the entry and recursively calls ConsoleStringRenderer.

Used for dynamic string selection, e.g. the item name or description for the item index in a RAM variable (item_name_table, item_description_table, ability_name_table, character_name_table, misc_ui_strings in system_strings).
ConsoleCmd_InsertRemoteString:
Recursively render a string from another bank.

3-byte operand (text tag [STR:@address]): 2-byte address + 1-byte bank. Takes the current cursor from the saved X on the stack, sets the data bank to the operand's bank (PHB, then PLB from a pushed byte), then calls ConsoleStringRenderer recursively via JSL with the new string address in Y. After return, restores the bank, advances Y past the 3-byte operand and stores the new cursor back.
ConsoleCmd_InsertSharedWord:
Insert a shared word from shared_word_table (text tag [LU:n]).

1-byte operand: entry index 0–$E. Multiplies by 2 (ASL) for the word table offset, switches the data bank to shared_word_table's bank, loads the string pointer and recursively calls ConsoleStringRenderer to render it (e.g. [LU:C] = 'Statue ', [LU:8] = 'Psycho '). Used by item names, item and ability descriptions and the ability menu. Returns the new cursor in the saved X on the stack.
ConsoleCmd_NewLine:
Line break of one tilemap row (text tag [N]).

Adds $0040 (64 bytes = 32 words = one 32-tile tilemap row) to the line start in $09A0 and writes the result to both $09A0 and the saved X on the stack ($03,S). The old cursor column is discarded: text continues in the column of the last position command. The step is one tilemap row; ConsoleCmd_DoubleNewLine below advances two.

No operand bytes consumed.
ConsoleCmd_Print3DigitNumber:
Format and print a decimal number as up to 3 digits.

2-byte operand: address of a 16-bit source value (in the current data bank, see the header). Extracts hundreds, tens, and ones digits via repeated subtraction (÷100, ÷10, ÷1). Each digit is OR'd with the $099E attribute word + $30 tile base (the '0' glyph).

Leading zero suppression: hundreds digit is replaced with blank tile $2000 if zero. Tens digit is blank only if hundreds was also zero (tracked via $0006 flag). Ones digit is always displayed.

The hundreds digit is clamped to 9, but the tens and ones still come from value mod 100, so 1005 prints 905 (not 999). Always writes 3 tiles and moves the cursor past them.
ConsoleCmd_PrintBcdNumber:
Print a packed BCD number with leading zero suppression.

3-byte operand (text tag [BCD:count,addr]): 1-byte digit count + 2-byte source address (current data bank, so a RAM variable). Digits are read from packed BCD bytes (2 digits per byte, least significant byte first, low nibble first) and printed right-to-left from cursor + 2×count. Each tile is $30 + digit in the low byte with the attribute byte $099F as the high byte ($099E's low byte is overwritten, not ORed).

After printing all digits, a suppression pass replaces leading '0' tiles ($30) with tile $20, always leaving the last digit. The cursor is advanced past the number. Every vanilla use is a 1-digit number, so the suppression pass has no vanilla effect; the project's string map names tile $20 '.', which is probably a blank in the actual font (unverified).
ConsoleCmd_PrintEquipIcons:
Print equipment item icons as 2×2 metatiles.

Variable-length operand (text tag [UNK], no use in any vanilla string): a list of 1-byte equipment indices terminated by any byte with bit 7 set (>= $80). Each item produces a 2×2 tile icon:
- Items 0-7: tile $01E0 + 2 × index (first equipment page)
- Items 8+: tile $02E0 + 2 × (index − 8) (second page)

The 4 tiles of each icon are N and N+1 in the row above the cursor and N+$10 and N+$11 in the cursor row (the sheet is 16 tiles wide). The cursor advances 4 bytes (2 tiles) per icon. A counter on the stack tracks the number of icons so Y can skip the operand and its terminator.
ConsoleCmd_PrintRawBytes:
Output raw tile bytes from the string until a $FF terminator.

Variable-length operand terminated by $FF (text tag [ESC:b1,b2,...]). Each byte is zero-extended to 16 bits, OR'd with the $099E attribute word, and written as a tile word to the VRAM buffer; this reaches tile indices below $12, which the main loop treats as commands (e.g. tiles 1–5 in the HUD string at consolestring_01E7F6). The $FF terminator is consumed but not written. The cursor is advanced past the run.
ConsoleCmd_SetPalette:
Set the palette attribute for subsequent tile writes.

1-byte operand (text tag [PAL:n], n is the already-shifted bit pattern, e.g. 4 = palette 1, 8 = palette 2, $14 = palette 5). Reads sceneStateHelper ($099F), clears the palette bits 2-4 (AND $E3), ORs the operand into them and writes back, so the priority bit (bit 5) and flips are kept. This sets the attribute byte of all following tiles.
ConsoleCmd_SetVramAddr:
Set the VRAM buffer write position from a 2-byte operand.

Reads a 16-bit buffer offset from the string data (text tag [POS:lo,hi]), stores it in both $09A0 (line start, used by the line-break commands) and the saved X on the stack ($03,S), which becomes X when the command returns. Advances Y past the 2-byte operand.
ConsoleStringCommandTable:
18-entry word table of command handler addresses for the Console string renderer.

Indexed by command byte (0–$11), each entry is a 16-bit JSR target (same bank). Entries cover text positioning, string insertion, number formatting, HP bars, equipment icons, and UI box drawing.
ConsoleStringRenderer:
Main entry point for the Console string rendering engine.

Called via JSL with Y = string data pointer, X = VRAM buffer byte offset into $7F0200. Saves processor state and data bank (restored by ConsoleCmd_End); it never changes the data bank itself, only the commands that recurse do. Processes the bytecode stream in a loop:
- Bytes >= $12: literal tile characters — written to VRAM buffer as a 16-bit tilemap word (low byte = tile index, high byte = attribute from sceneStateHelper $099F)
- Bytes $00–$11: command opcodes — dispatched via indexed indirect JSR through ConsoleStringCommandTable

The X register (VRAM write position) is pushed around each command (PHX/PLX), so a command that moves the cursor writes the new position into the pushed copy ($03,S).
CopyPaletteBundleFrame:
Apply one palette-bundle frame: copy a block of colors from ROM into the palette staging buffer (not a decompression, and no VRAM is touched).

Programs the RAM block-move stub at $0402 (PHB / MVN / PLB / RTS, written by system_init): one 16-bit store of $967F puts $7F in $0404 (MVN destination bank) and $96 in $0405 (source bank, the palette_bundles bank). Then A = $7F0008,X (frame size − 1), Y = metaspritePtr (destination offset in bank $7F), X = chatPtr (source offset in bank $96) and JSR $0402. MVN leaves X one past the last source byte; it is stored back to chatPtr, so the next call copies the following frame of the strip to the same destination. The caller's X is saved around the call.

The NMI later uploads the $7F0A00 staging buffer to CGRAM (UploadCgramPalette) and the backdrop triplet at $7F0C00 to the fixed color; this routine only edits those RAM mirrors.
CrashCameraController:
Companion thinker driving camera scroll, gravity acceleration, and scene transition.

Three-phase thinker spawned via SpawnBefore, running before the main crash actor each frame.

Phase 1 — Approach (600 frames):
- Set render flag $0800 in actor flags ($10)
- Timer = $0258 (600 frames)
- Mode 7 center X = cameraTargetX + $80 → $00CA
- Rotation angle = $0200 → $00B6, scale = $0032 → $00B8, perspective = 0 → $00BC
- Per-frame: scroll cameraTargetY up by 2, compute Y center = (cameraTargetY & $03FF) + $70 → $00CC
- Decrement timer; continue until timer < 0

Phase 2 — Signal + scroll (60 frames):
- SetFlagByte #01 (tells main actor to enter exit phase)
- Loop 60 more frames of continued camera scroll
- SpawnAfterFlags CrashDebrisSfx with $2000 flags

Phase 3 — Gravity:
- InitGravity(0, 5, 0): vertical gravity at speed 5
- TickGravity loop: add velocity (moveScratch2) to Mode 7 scale ($00B8)
- Continue camera scroll each frame
- When scale ≥ $0500 (loc_03A1AF): trigger scene transition
  - Set game flag $0AA6 = 1 (marks garden crash in game state)
  - Set gfxCacheIdxB = $0404 (post-crash graphics)
  - QueueMapChange to scene $58 with params ($0000, $0000, $80, $1100)
  - Continue gravity + camera scroll for smooth visual exit
CrashDebrisSfx:
Crash debris sound effect actor — 6 random sound bursts.

Spawned via SpawnAfterFlags with $2000 flags during the gravity phase. Loops 6 times: each iteration generates a random byte, masks to $1C (values 0/4/8/12/16/20/24/28) and stores to $08 as an animation/frame offset, then plays sound #15 (crash/impact). Dies after all 6 iterations.
DecomposeActorMetasprites:
Expand a generic actor's metasprite definition into individual OAM entries.

Switches DBR to the actor's sprite bank ($7F0008,X). Computes screen-relative position by subtracting scroll offsets ($1A, $1E) from the actor's world position minus origin ($14-$18, $16-$1A). Loads the OAM attribute word ($000E,X → $04) for mirror detection.

Iframe blinking: only when actor flag $0080 (iframe/hit-reaction active, set by ApplyPlayerHitstun together with the counter) is set and $0010 is clear: if the iframe counter ($7F0028,X) is nonzero and its low bit is set (LSR carry; the counter counts each frame, so the flash alternates — inferred), sets palette override $02 = $0E00 (palette 7) to produce the flash.

Dispatches to DecomposePlayerSprites if bit 15 ($8000) of $10 is set (player actor).

For generic actors: reads the metasprite pointer ($7F000C,X + 8), extracts the sub-sprite count from byte 0, then iterates each 7-byte sub-sprite entry. For each sub-sprite:
1. Y offset: read bytes 3-4 (XBA if V-mirrored), add screen Y ($1C), bounds-check < $F0
2. Tile/attribute: read bytes 5-6, EOR with the attribute word ($04), OR with palette override ($02)
3. X offset: read bytes 1-2 (XBA if H-mirrored), add screen X ($18), bounds-check < $110
4. Write OAM low-table entry and pack hi-table bits
5. Advance to next sub-sprite (+7 bytes) or bail if OAM full (Y = $0200)

Off-screen sub-sprites do not consume an OAM slot: $E080 is written over the current slot only to scrub any partly written entry, and the next sub-sprite reuses it. Returns carry set when OAM is full (128 entries), carry clear otherwise.
DecomposePlayerSprites:
Expand the player character's metasprite into OAM entries with VRAM tile remapping.

Calls CheckPlayerSpriteCache to detect metasprite/bank changes. Loads the character form ($0AD4) and computes a body table index (form × 6 via ASL+ADC+ASL). If playerFlags bit 15 is set (transformation/override), uses animScratch2 ($7F000E,X) directly as the body table index instead.

From the body table (6 bytes per form): the word at +3 is the tile graphics source address, stored to $06FC; the byte at +5 is its bank, stored as the first byte of the tile-DMA list at $06FE (DmaPlayerTilesToVram reads it back as the DMA source bank). Then reads the metasprite at the cached pointer ($09CC + 8) and iterates sub-sprites similarly to DecomposeActorMetasprites, with two additions:

1. Tile source remapping: each sub-sprite's tile number is multiplied by 32 (AND $01FF, ASL ×5, 32 bytes per 4bpp tile) and added to $06FC to give the RAM address of that tile's graphics; the address is appended to the list at ($08) for DMA.
2. Sequential OAM tile numbering ($14): the OAM tile written for each sub-sprite is $14, which grows by 2 per sub-sprite. When it reaches $10 it jumps by $10 more, skipping the tile rows $10–$1F that hold the lower halves of the first eight sprites (VRAM $4100); sprites 9 and up land in the $4200 overflow region.

On completion, writes $0000 to ($08) as the list terminator.
DeferSceneTransition: Callback after the menu handler. Route id 0 means the player chose Quit (the handler queued the scene they came from), so it just dies and the normal scene change happens. Otherwise it moves the queued destination into $0D6E (low byte only, $0D6F keeps the source scene) and $0652 into $0D6C, then clears both so the scene does not change until the route has played.
DialogCmd_AdvanceCursor: Command with a 1-byte operand: the amount is rounded down to an even byte count (whole tile words) and added to the VRAM buffer cursor X, which is also stored to $0998. An amount of 0 or 1 does nothing.
DialogCmd_ClearBox:
Clear the box interior without removing borders.

Fills the interior region with blank tiles ($2040) in both tile rows ($7F0200 and $7F0240). Clears 2w interior columns and h text lines (counters 2w−1 and h−1 with BPL loops, i.e. one extra pass each); each pass writes the top and bottom tile rows and advances $80 bytes (two 32-tile rows). Resets cursor to box origin and line counter to 0.
DialogCmd_ClearDialogueBox:
Clear the entire dialogue box and reset rendering state.

Resets the VRAM cursor to the box origin ($099A). Zeroes every tile of the box including its border: 2w+2 columns by 2h+3 tile rows (w, h = $0982/$0984), starting one column left and one row above the content origin (the BPL loops run one extra pass). Restores the default dialogue palette: writes $675D (white), $10F2 (shadow), $0000 (transparent) to the CGRAM mirror at $7F0A22–$7F0A27 (CGRAM colors $11–$13). Triggers display update, resets cursor and line counter ($099C).
DialogCmd_DictionaryA:
Insert a word from dictionary A (dialog_dictionaries.dialog_dictionary_a).

Reads a 1-byte index, doubles it for the word pointer table, switches DBR to the dictionary bank, reads the string pointer, and recursively renders via JSL DialogStringRenderer. Used for common words to save space in dialogue scripts.
DialogCmd_DictionaryB:
Insert a word from dictionary B (dialog_dictionaries.dialog_dictionary_b).

Identical to DictionaryA but reads from the second dictionary table. Two dictionaries allow more than 256 common words while keeping operands to 1 byte each.
DialogCmd_EndAndWait: End-of-dialogue command: waits for a button press, clears the dialogue box, clears the D-pad bits ($0F00) from the joypadHeld consumption mask so directional input is live again, and restores the saved frame delay from $0B04 to $007E.
DialogCmd_IndirectString:
Render a string selected from an indirect pointer table.

Reads a 4-byte operand: bytes 0-1 = base pointer offset, bytes 2-3 = table address. Computes the string pointer as: table[base[table_addr]] + base_offset. Then recursively renders via JSL DialogStringRenderer.
DialogCmd_InfiniteLoop: Command that spins on a BRA to itself, deliberately halting the dialogue engine (NOPs pad the loop).
DialogCmd_InsertRemoteString: Command with a 3-byte operand (address, bank): saves the cursor to $0998, switches DBR to the operand bank, calls DialogStringRenderer recursively on that string, then restores the cursor and DBR and skips the operand.
DialogCmd_InsertTemplate:
Recursively render a template string from the dialog_template_table pointer table.

Reads a 1-byte operand (template index), multiplies by 2 for the word-sized pointer table, switches DBR to the template bank, and calls DialogStringRenderer recursively via JSL. Restores the caller's string pointer, bank and processor flags on return, and reloads the VRAM cursor from $0998, where the template's last character left it (DialogCmd_Return hands the cursor back only through $0998), so a [DLG] template positions the text that follows.
DialogCmd_JumpToAddress: Command with a 2-byte operand: loads it into Y so the character loop continues at that address in the current bank.
DialogCmd_NewLine:
Advance to the next line within the dialogue box.

Increments the line counter ($099C). If it equals the box height ($0984), scrolls the dialogue up by two tile rows (two ScrollDialogueUp passes with a WaitOneFrame after each), the line counter then stays on the last line. Computes the new VRAM cursor position: base ($099A) + line × $80 bytes (two 32-tile BG3 rows per text line). Updates both X and $0998.
DialogCmd_OpenDefaultBox:
Open the standard dialogue box used for most NPC conversations.

Hardcoded dimensions: 13 columns × 4 rows, positioned at column 3, row 17 (bottom of screen). Computes the VRAM buffer offset and jumps to OpenDialogueBox_Body to share the box construction logic with DialogCmd_OpenDialogueBox.
DialogCmd_OpenDialogueBox:
Open a custom-sized dialogue box with border and interior.

Reads 2-byte operand: byte 0 = width (columns), byte 1 = height (rows). Stores dimensions to $0982/$0984. Falls through to OpenDialogueBox_Body which constructs the box frame using DialogueBorderTiles, fills the interior via DrawDialogueBodyRows, and triggers a display update. Skips the WaitOneFrame at the end for scene $FA (the diary menu, sFA_diary_menu).
DialogCmd_PrintNumber:
Print a packed-BCD number as digit tiles.

Reads a 4-byte operand: word 0 = number of digits to print, word 1 = address of the number data. The data is little-endian 16-bit words holding four nibbles each (word 0 = lowest four digits); the digits are printed most-significant first.

Stack frame (6 words above the saved Y): SP+1 = data address, SP+3 = digit count, SP+5 = nibble position within the current word (1–4, 4 = highest), SP+7 = digits already handled, SP+9 = word index, SP+B = digits-printed flag. Each pass derives the position from (count − handled): repeated subtraction of 4 gives the word index and position, the word is fetched from data + 2 × index, and LSR ×4 per position moves the nibble into the low bits.

The nibble is mapped through HexDigitTileTable and written to both tile rows. Leading zeros are suppressed until the first nonzero digit, except that a zero at position 1 is always printed (the last digit of the number, but also the lowest nibble of any higher word: with more than 4 digits that prints a leading zero — E1 analysis, unverified at runtime). Each digit calls WaitNFrames_PerChar for the typing effect.
DialogCmd_PrintRawTiles:
Output raw tile bytes directly until a zero terminator.

Reads bytes from the string stream one at a time. Each nonzero byte is OR'd with palette and priority bits and written to both VRAM buffer rows. Zero byte terminates. Used for rendering pre-composed tile sequences (icons, special characters).
DialogCmd_Return: Exit the wide-string renderer. Saves the VRAM cursor back to $0998, unwinds the renderer's stack frame, then RTL returns to the caller. The first PLX discards the PEA'd loop return address left by the command dispatch; the second restores the caller's X (pushed at entry); PLD and PLP restore DP and flags. The updated cursor is handed back only through $0998.
DialogCmd_SetFrameDelay:
Set the per-character typing delay.

Reads a 1-byte operand, adds 2 (INC INC), masks to byte, and stores to $007E. The +2 bias means operand 0 = 2-frame delay, operand 1 = 3-frame delay, etc. A value of 0 in $007E (from the BEQ check in WaitNFrames_PerChar) causes instant rendering.
DialogCmd_SetPalette:
Set the tile palette for subsequent characters.

Reads a 1-byte palette index, swaps bytes (XBA) and shifts left 2 (ASL ×2) to position palette bits in the VRAM tile word format (bits 12-10). Stores to $0986 which is OR'd into every tile written by the character loop.
DialogCmd_SetPaletteColor:
Write a single 15-bit color value directly to the CGRAM palette buffer.

Reads 3-byte operand: byte 0 = palette index (×2 for word offset), bytes 1-2 = 15-bit BGR color value. Writes to $7F0A00 + index×2. Used for dialogue-specific color effects.
DialogCmd_SetPosition:
Set the dialogue cursor to a specific (column, row) position.

Reads a 2-byte operand: low byte = column → $097A, high byte = row → $097C. Computes the VRAM buffer byte offset as row×$40 + column×2: XBA + LSR + LSR makes row×$40 (row << 8 >> 2), then the column is added twice. Updates both X register and $0998.
DialogCmd_SetSfx: Command with a 1-byte operand: stores it as the per-character sound effect ID in $0996.
DialogCmd_WaitForAnyInput:
Wait for a press of any button in mask $C040 (see DialogCmd_WaitForButton).

Marks $C040 as consumed in joypadHeld, then loops WaitOneFrame until one of those bits appears in joypadCurrent. The pressed bits are stored in joypadHeld (consumed) and the command returns without drawing a cursor or clearing the box.
DialogCmd_WaitForButton:
Wait for a confirm/cancel press with a blinking cursor indicator.

Marks the button mask $C040 as consumed in joypadHeld (so a button already held when the command starts is ignored until released and pressed again), then loops WaitOneFrame until one of those bits appears in joypadCurrent. $C040 = logical bits $8000, $4000 and $0040, the confirm, cancel and item-palette buttons after the remap stage (see the diary-menu layouts and vblank_joypad); it excludes the attack bit $0080. While waiting it draws a blinking cursor via DrawDialogueCursor (carry set = animate). On a press, the pressed bits are stored in joypadHeld (consumed), the cursor is erased (carry clear), and DialogCmd_ClearBox prepares the next page.
DialogCmd_WaitFrames: Command with a 1-byte operand: waits that many frames through WaitNFrames_Entry, then skips the operand byte.
dialogstring_03B928: Blank [TPL:11] string, like dialogstring_03B92B. Nothing references it.
DialogStringCommandTable: Command handler table: 25 word offsets (bank $03), indexed by (opcode AND $1F) × 2. Opcodes $C0–$D8 map to entries 00–18. There is no range check, so opcodes $D9–$DF would read past the table into the code that follows; whether any string uses them was not checked.
DialogStringRenderer:
Main bytecode interpreter for the wide-string dialogue format.

Entry: JSL with Y = string data pointer (read through DBR). The VRAM buffer cursor is taken from $0998, not from the caller's X, which is only saved and restored. Sets DP = 0 for zero-page scratch access.

The character loop (DialogString_CharLoop) reads one byte at a time from [Y]. Bytes < $C0 are treated as tile indices: masked to 8 bits, OR'd with palette bits ($0986) and priority ($2100), then written to both $7F0200,X (top tile row) and $7F0240,X (bottom row, +$10 offset). The cursor X advances by 2 per character.

Bytes ≥ $C0 are command opcodes: masked to 5 bits (AND #$001F), doubled as a word index, looked up in DialogStringCommandTable, and dispatched via an RTS trick (PEA loop_addr−1, push cmd_addr−1, RTS).

After each visible character: if worldReadyFlag is set, calls WaitNFrames_PerChar for the typing delay, checks for the ellipsis tile ($AC) to suppress sound, and queues the per-character SFX ($0996) to sfxQueueCh1.
DialogueBorderTiles: Border tile words for the dialogue box, in the order the draw routines consume them: top row (left corner, edge, right corner = H-flipped corner), body sides (left, right = H-flipped), bottom row (left corner V-flipped, edge V-flipped, right corner H+V-flipped). $2000 is the BG priority bit; $4000/$8000 are H/V flip.
DmaPlayerTiles_LowerHalf:
DMA inner loop — transfer lower tile rows for the player sprite.

Same structure as DmaPlayerTiles_UpperHalf but operates in 16-bit mode to add $0200 to each source pointer before transfer. This offset reaches the lower half of each 16×16 tile's graphics data in the source buffer. Restores 8-bit mode on exit.
DmaPlayerTiles_UpperHalf: Transfer up to 8 upper-half tile rows to VRAM. Reads word pointers from the playerTileDmaBank list starting at Y (from $06FF), programs one 64-byte DMA per pointer (A1T0 = pointer, DAS0 = $40) and stops when Y reaches $11 (8 entries) or a pointer is zero. Y is not reset between the first and the continuation pass.
DmaPlayerTilesToVram:
Transfer player character sprite tiles from RAM to VRAM during V-Blank.

Checks displayModeFlags bit 3 ($08) — returns immediately if not set (no pending tile update). Clears the flag after entry to prevent re-triggering.

Sets up DMA channel 0 in word-increment mode (VMAIN=$80, DMAP0=$01, BBAD0=$18) with the source bank from $06FE. Transfers tiles in four passes:
1. Upper-half tiles to VRAM $4000 via DmaPlayerTiles_UpperHalf
2. If all 8 tile entries consumed (Y=$11): upper-half continuation to VRAM $4200
3. Lower-half tiles to VRAM $4100 via DmaPlayerTiles_LowerHalf
4. If all 8 entries consumed: lower-half continuation to VRAM $4300

The tile source table at $06FE contains up to 8 word-sized pointers. Each pointer is a RAM address holding 64 bytes ($40) of tile data (one 16×16 metatile = four 8×8 tiles). The lower half adds $0200 to each source address to reach the bottom tile rows.

Used by both ClearSceneState (scene loading) and the NMI handler (per-frame animation updates).
DotAnimationLoop: Shared dot loop (leader and companions). Every frame the dot is placed at camera + slot pair; while a route is playing the frame hold time (from $08 into $26) counts down and AnimOneFrame stages the next animation frame. When the route id becomes 0 the dot moves one step toward its home pair and dies, so all dots are gone as soon as the route ends. The leader's home is its own slot, so it dies at once.
DotMoveHome: Not at home yet: the Y target is the high byte of orbitDiameter ($7F0013) + cameraTargetY, one MoveToward step toward home, then Die.
DotNextCycle: Animation timer expired: restart the shared dot loop.
DotRouteEnded: Route id is 0 (the route is over): the home X is the low byte of orbitDiameter + cameraTargetX; when the dot is already there the Y test follows and the dot dies, otherwise it goes to DotMoveHome.
DrawDialogueBodyRows:
Fill the interior rows of the dialogue box.

For each row: draws the left border tile, fills the interior with blank tiles ($2040), and draws the right border tile. Decrements the height counter $1C. After all body rows, draws one more blank row (same left/fill/right pattern) if worldReadyFlag is set and the menu-mode flag $00EE is zero; this row holds the continuation cursor (DrawDialogueCursor) and supplies the blank source row when ScrollDialogueUp shifts the text. Advances the tile pointer past the border data (+4 bytes).
DrawDialogueBorderRow:
Render one horizontal border row of the dialogue box.

Reads three tiles from the border tile pointer [$3E]: left corner, repeated middle tile (width times), and right corner. Writes directly to the VRAM staging buffer at $7F0200,X. Advances the tile pointer by 6 bytes (3 words) for the next border set.
DrawDialogueCursor:
Draw or erase the blinking continuation cursor below the text area, horizontally centred in the dialogue box.

Carry flag controls mode: SEC = animate (blink), CLC = erase. In animate mode $0994 is incremented once every 16 frames (whenever the low nibble of the global frame counter $36 is 0, assuming one call per frame) and its bit 0 selects the tile: odd = cursor tile ($2091), even = blank ($2040), so the cursor blinks with a 32-frame period. Erase mode writes the blank tile.

The position formula: X = ((2h + row_origin) × 32 + w + column_origin) × 2 bytes into $7F0200, where w, h = $0982/$0984 and row/column origin = $0980/$097E. That is the extra blank row just below the 2h text rows, at the middle of the 2w-wide text area.
DrawHpBar:
Shared HP bar rendering routine used by both player and enemy HP commands.

Takes the cursor (buffer offset) in A, sets Y = 10 (tiles left in the row). Draws segments in order:
1. Full segments ($00 count): tile $2006 | $04
2. Half segment ($08 flag): tile $2007 | $04 (skipped if 0)
3. Empty segments ($02 count): tile $20FF | $04
4. Blank tiles ($0000): the rest of the first 10-tile row (unless the bar already wrapped), then the rest of the second row, so a shrinking bar erases its old tiles

When Y reaches 0 (10 tiles drawn), HpBar_AdvanceRow moves to the next tilemap row and resets Y. $04 ($0800 = player, $0400 = enemy) is OR'd into each segment tile. It does not return the cursor: the HP commands leave the caller's cursor unchanged, so text after [HP]/[HE] continues where the bar started.
DrawMenuCursor:
Draw the menu selection cursor with a 16-frame blink animation.

Increments the blink counter ($0994). Bit 4 determines the cursor phase: clear = highlight tiles ($212C/$213C for top/bottom), set = dim tiles ($21AC both). Saves the tiles currently under the cursor to $0990/$0992, then overwrites with cursor tiles.

Computes the cursor position from: the base row offset (SP+6), the grid selection index (SP+3), the column count (from packed dimensions), and the box origin ($097E/$0980). The X offset ($18) is 0 for the first page or $18 for the second page.
EmitDigitOamEntry:
Write one digit sprite to the OAM compose buffer.

Digit value in A (0–9). Adds $70 to convert to a tile index (digit font starts at tile $70), ORs in the attribute word from DP $0002. Writes X ($0018), Y ($001C) and the tile word to the buffer at $7F3100 + $00D8 (offsets +0, +2, +4) and advances the cursor by 6 bytes.
ExecuteSceneTransition:
Main scene transition orchestrator — handles the full scene change sequence.

Three-phase operation:

=== PHASE 1: EXIT ===
If worldReadyFlag is positive (world active and visible): runs ScreenExitTransition for the visual fade/dissolve effect, then clears worldReadyFlag to 0. If it is already 0 the exit transition is skipped. If it is negative (bit 7 set) both the exit and the enter transition are skipped and the flag is left unchanged — no writer of a negative value exists in the extracted code (only $0000 and $000F are stored), so this path looks unused (inferred). Then clears the HDMA enable mask ($66), disables NMI (joypad auto-read only) and enters forced blank.

=== PHASE 2: RESOLVE TARGET SCENE ===
Two paths:
- $0D52/$0D53 nonzero (staged world-map entry): Archives the staged word $0D52 → $0D54 (the world-map player start X; start Y $0D56 is already staged) and $0652 → $0D6C (deferred auxiliary data), clearing both sources. Saves sceneNext in $0D6E (deferred destination scene) and sceneCurrent in $0D6F (the scene being left; WorldMapController reads $0D6F as the area ID). Sets the new scene ID to $FE (world map).
- sceneNext nonzero (normal transition): Records the scene being left (sceneCurrent) in $0D6E, clears $0D6F. Uses sceneNext as the new scene ID.

Stores the resolved scene to sceneCurrent and computes the doubled scene index ($0646) for table lookups.

=== PHASE 3: LOAD ===
Calls ClearSceneState (the comprehensive scene setup), LoadHudTilemap, UpdateHUD, and a chain of VBlank sync/NMI enable calls. The last call of the chain, EnableNmiAndJoypad, leaves NMITIMEN = $81 into the enter transition: the first UpdateFrameDialogue pass runs RunActors_CutsceneOnly with the NMI on, and the DisableNmiKeepJoypad at the end of that pass turns it off. Runs ScreenEnterTransition unless worldReadyFlag was already nonzero, then sets worldReadyFlag to $000F (fully ready). Clears gfxCacheIdxA/B (the transition parameters).

If $00B4 is nonzero (DisplaySceneTitle sets it to $E0 when it opens the scene-title box): enters a wait loop calling UpdateFrameDialogue until any button is pressed, then clears $00B4/$00B5, clears the staging buffer below the HUD rows (ClearBg3TilemapBuffer_PreserveHud, which removes the title box), and sets displayModeFlags bit 0 so the buffer is flushed.

Finally clears joypadInject and $09AD before returning.
FluteControllerExit: Cleanup for FluteMusicActorController: clears displayModeFlags bit $0080 (leave display-filter mode) and COP Die; reached on spawn failure and after restoration wait.
FluteMusicActorController:
Multi-phase music playback actor for melody items.

Orchestrates the complete melody playback lifecycle shared by Wind Melody, Lola's Melody, and Memory Melody:

Phase 1 — Setup: Enter display-filter mode (displayModeFlags $0080), store the original music ID from musicParentActor into DP $24, spawn SpcTransferMusicData to upload the melody's music data to the SPC700. If spawn fails (Y=$1FC0 = pool full), jump to FluteControllerExit and die. Otherwise swap X/Y registers to configure the spawned music actor: store track number (+1) in chatPtr, set the display-filter bit ($1000 in $12). Give the player actor the same bit, override it to a static idle pose (PlayerStaticBodyPose via SetPlayerTransition), set playerFlags $0800 (script/ability lock), and hide the buttons (joypadMaskStd |= $CFFC). Yield and poll each frame until musicTransitionState == $FFFF.

Phase 2 — Playback: Poll APUIO1 ($2141) each frame. When the SPC signals $FF (track finished), clear the display-filter bit from the player actor, restore the player to normal pose (PlayerWalkingIdlePose), unhide the buttons, and dispatch to the melody-specific *_Effect handler via SwitchCase on DP $20 (melody index 0/1/2).

Phase 3 — Restoration (FluteRestoreMusicPhase): After the effect handler, spawn another SpcTransferMusicData to restore the original background music. Wait for musicTransitionState == $FFFF again, delay 2 ticks (WaitByte #01 = N + 1), then fall through into FluteControllerExit.

Cleanup (FluteControllerExit): Reached by that fall-through and by the jump on spawn failure — clears displayModeFlags $0080 (leaves display-filter mode) and dies.
FlutePlaybackPhase: Phase 2 entry of FluteMusicActorController after musicTransitionState is $FFFF: SetEntryHere polls APUIO1 each frame until $FF signals the melody finished, then clears player display-filter, restores walking idle pose, unmasks joypad, and SwitchCases on melody index into the effect handlers with return set to FluteRestoreMusicPhase.
FluteRestoreMusicPhase: Phase 3 after the melody effect: spawns SpcTransferMusicData with chatPtr from saved DP $24, polls until musicTransitionState is $FFFF again, WaitByte #01 (2 ticks), then falls through into FluteControllerExit.
FormatDamageDigits:
Convert a 16-bit damage number to packed BCD digit format for sprite display.

Input: damage value on stack. Output: packed BCD in A (carry clear = success).

Values ≥ 1000 ($03E8): returns carry set (overflow — too many digits).

For values < 1000: extracts hundreds digit via repeated subtraction by 100/500. Switches to 8-bit for tens and ones: repeated subtraction by 50/10. Packs result as: high byte = hundreds digit, bits 7-4 of low byte = tens, bits 3-0 = ones.

The packed format matches what SpawnDamageNumberEffect expects for rendering individual digit sprites as floating damage numbers.

formation_leader_plus_4: Five pairs for N = 4: same as the first five pairs of formation_leader_plus_5 (the entry is redundant).

FutureVisionController:
Companion thinker driving the 5-phase vision sequence.

Phase 1 — Init + zoom-in with rotation:
- Camera position ($0170,$01D0), M7 center ($01F0,$0250)
- Scale $001C, perspective $0130
- Spawns oneshot_palette_flash_19 thinker for visual flash
- Per-frame: INC $BC (rotate). On even frames only (skip odd via $0036 & 1): INC $B8 (zoom in)
- Zoom-in runs until scale reaches $0080 (~200 frames at half-speed)

Phase 2 — Full rotation wait (loc_03A277):
- New yield point via SetEntryHere
- Per-frame: check ($BC & $01FF) == 0 (full 512-step rotation)
- INC $BC each frame until complete

Phase 3 — Hold + zoom-out with scroll (loc_03A285):
- WaitByte $77: 119-frame pause
- Per-frame zoom-out: DEC $B8 from $80 → $60 (32 frames)
- Simultaneously: INC $B6 (rotation angle), INC cameraTargetY ×2, INC $CC ×2 (camera + M7 center scroll down by 2px/frame)

Phase 4 — Long upward scroll + brightness fade (loc_03A2A6):

- Loop $80 (128): continued scroll
- Loop $7F (127): scroll + INIDISP brightness fade. Extracts bits 3-6 of loopCounter via AND $0078 >> 3, producing 16-step fade from $0F to $00 (8 frames per brightness level)

Phase 5 — Scene transition:
- QueueMapChange to scene $BF at ($00F8,$00C0), params ($00, $2200)
- gfxCacheIdxA = $0001, gfxCacheIdxB = $0400
- Final yield + RTL

2. Configure Mode 7 color math: M7SEL=0, TM=$01 (BG1 main), CGADSUB=$01, CGWSEL=$82
