GardenCrashCutscene:
Sky Garden crash cutscene actor-def — Mode 7 init, companion spawning, and animation loop.

Init phase:
1. Mask joypad ($FFF0) to disable UI buttons during cutscene
2. Configure Mode 7 color math: M7SEL=0, TS=$01, CGADSUB=$01, CGWSEL=$82
3. SpawnThinker Mode7PerspectiveUpdate for per-scanline rotation HDMA
4. Write $0804 to thinker's animScratch2 (rotation/scale speed params)
5. SpawnBefore CrashCameraController as companion (runs before this actor each frame)
6. Position sprite at cameraTargetX + $80, stage sprite config #04

Main loop (loc_03A0E7): two-yield cycle per iteration. First yield: animate one frame, copy animation result ($08) to timer ($24), clear $08. Second yield: position at cameraTargetY + $B4. Check flag byte #01 — when set by CrashCameraController, branch to GardenCrashExitPhase. Otherwise decrement $24; if negative, loop back. If non-negative, return (wait for next frame).
GardenCrashExitPhase:
Terminal animation phase — 30-frame fadeout after camera signals completion.

Entered when CrashCameraController sets flag byte #01 (approach + gravity phases complete). SetEntryExit marks this as a terminal state. Loops 30 frames ($1E): each frame animates one step and positions at cameraTargetY + $B4, tracking the still-scrolling camera. After the loop, one final yield + RTL ends the actor.
GetPlayerFacing_BaseBodyFallback: Fallback target for the sprite-override path (not an external entry point; the only reference is the BMI at 258301). Reached when playerFlags bit 15 is set but $0AC8 − 4 is negative (body_table index 0–3, the base bodies): it discards the extra pushed Y and rejoins the normal FacingDirectionLookup path at loc_03F0D6. The form-table code that follows it (loc_03F0F1) is the real sprite-override path, entered by the BMI at 258260.
GetPlayerFacingDirection:
Get the player's facing direction from animation frame.

Loads the player actor's animation frame ($0028,X) and looks up its direction in FacingDirectionLookup (or the per-form table when playerFlags bit 15 is set). Returns 0–3 with carry clear, or carry set if the table value is ≥ 4 (no facing). The caller's X is parked in Y for the call and restored before RTL; P is saved and restored too.
GiveItem_DefUp: DEF Up (item $82): clears displayModeFlags bit $0080, plays SFX $25, adds 1 to playerDef (8-bit; an old value of $7F becomes $55), Y = 0, then returns through GiveItem_Success.
GiveItem_InventoryFull: Return from GiveItemToPlayer when inventory is full. Pops item ID from stack, stores at $0DB8 for dialogue display. Sets Y to the inventory-full dialogue string pointer. Returns with carry set.
GiveItem_StoreInSlot: Store regular item in inventory. Pops item ID from stack, writes to inventorySlots[Y] (first empty slot found by GiveItemToPlayer). Stores item ID at $0DB8 for dialogue display. Sets Y to the item-get success dialogue string pointer. Falls through to GiveItem_Success.
GiveItem_Success: Return from GiveItemToPlayer with success. Restores processor flags and returns with carry clear.
GiveItemToPlayer:
Give the item whose id is in A (low byte). Regular ids $00 to $7F go into the first empty slot of inventorySlots; ids from $80 are specials, decoded as id - $80: 0 HP Max Up, 1 STR Up, 2 DEF Up (GiveItem_DefUp), 3 / 4 / 5 = 1 / 2 / 5 gems, 6 and up = heal 5 HP with the spark effect.
Returns carry clear = given, carry set = inventory full; Y = dialogue string for regular items and for the full case. Details in the block note.
GlobalInputHandler:
Per-frame overworld UI input dispatcher — routes Start, Select, and Y buttons to map, inventory, and item use.

Called from the main game loop each frame. Five guard conditions suppress input: pending scene transition (sceneNext nonzero), game over active ($0200), melody playing (IsMusicPlaying carry set), and guard/channel stance or script/ability lock ($2800) — though Start bypasses the $2800 guard.

Button priority: Start ($1000) is checked first → map/radar. Then $2800 guard. Then Select ($2000) → inventory. Then the item-use button (vanilla Y $4000, logical $0008 here) → item use.

=== MAP/RADAR PATH ===

Marks Start consumed in joypadHeld. Two sub-paths based on playerFlags bit 3 ($0008, combat lock):

- Normal (clear): RadarScreenSetup renders the full minimap with actors, markers, and enemy clear status. Enters the display loop at full brightness.
- Combat-locked (set): COP RunBg3Script displays 'PAUSE' text (consolestring_01EAC6). Clears displayModeFlags bit 15, enables NMI for one VBlank cycle, then sets INIDISP to $09 (dimmed). Enters the display loop.

Display loop: EnableNmiAndJoypad → VBlankWait → DisableNmiKeepJoypad → RadarBorderAnimate (the animation index lives in a word pushed on the stack, read by RadarBorderAnimate as $03,S) → poll joypadCurrent's high byte ($0657) for bit $10 (Start), which only reappears after Start is released and pressed again. On that press: re-consume Start in joypadHeld ($0659) so the closing press cannot reopen the map, clear overlay VRAM, restore brightness to $0F, set displayModeFlags bit 0 for VRAM flush, call UpdateFrameDialogue to restore display.

=== INVENTORY PATH ===

Marks Select consumed ($2000). VBlankWait → OpenInventoryScreen → DisableNmiKeepJoypad. On return, marks Select+Y ($6000, vanilla button values) consumed to prevent re-trigger.

=== ITEM USE PATH ===

Jumps directly to ItemUseDispatch. The JMP transfers control without pushing a return address — ItemUseDispatch handles its own cleanup and returns via the stacked PLP/RTL from this routine's PHP.
HitInvincibleVictim:
Handle enemy hitting a player that has the invincible flag ($0010).

Sets $0080 (iframe) in actor flags, assigns iframe counter $FFEF (recovery), checks onHitCallback for custom response. Plays invincible-hit sound #09 instead of normal damage sound. Then falls through to the enemy post-collision cleanup (loc_03C0E2) which handles extendedFlags $0050 and onCollideCallback processing.
HpBar_AdvanceRow:
Advance to the next VRAM row during HP bar rendering.

Adds $002C to X, which combined with the 10 tiles × 2 bytes already drawn ($14) equals one full tilemap row stride ($0040 = 64 bytes). Saves the new position to $06 as a row-continuation flag. Resets Y to 10 for the new row.

Guard: if the new X is $0100 or more (past buffer row 3), it pops an extra return address (PLA, discarding the return into DrawHpBar) so the RTS returns straight to DrawHpBar's caller and the rest of the bar is skipped.
HudTilemapData:
Static tilemap data for the in-game HUD display.

Contains 75 word entries (150 bytes) in the LoadHudTilemap stream format: tilemap words (tile index, palette and priority bits) interleaved with skip commands. Expanded, it covers 159 BG3 tilemap words (41 tiles, 118 skipped positions). The individual HUD glyphs have not been decoded.

Embedded skip commands (zero words) advance the cursor past empty regions of the HUD layout, avoiding the need to store blank tiles explicitly.
InitActorFromSceneData:
Parse a variable-length binary actor record from the scene data stream.

Reads sequentially from [$3E] with Y as the stream offset:
- Bytes 0-1: X/Y tile coordinates → ×16 (ASL ×4) → pixel positions at $0014,X and $0016,X
- Byte 2: Type/flags byte. Bit 0 selects how $000E,X (oamXorFlags) is built: 0 = ((byte2 & $F6) << 8) | word at $06F0 (default actor properties; never written by extracted code), 1 = direct mode (byte2 >> 1)
- Bytes 3-4: Code pointer → $42 (work area)
- Byte 5: Bank byte → $44
- Byte 6: Stats table index → $7F0020,X. Zero = no stats (skip enemy init)
- Byte 7: Enemy number → $7F0022,X. Used for defeat flag check
- Byte 8: Event-block index → $7F0024,X (deathActionIdx; swapped at spawn if the enemy is already defeated, and used by scripts as the event-block/flag index of a field reveal)

If enemy number is nonzero, calls CheckEnemyDefeatedFlag. If already defeated (carry set), jumps to AdvanceSceneDataAndFree to skip this actor and free the pool slot.

For actors with a stats index, sets bit 8 ($0100) in extended flags ($7F002A,X), reads byte 8, and increments the remaining-enemy counters enemiesRemaining ($0AEC, binary) and enemiesRemainingBcd ($0AEE, BCD via SED); the defeat handlers decrement them again.

Then parses the code header at [$42]: byte 0 = animation state ($0028,X), bytes 1-2 = initial flags (ORed with $4000 → $0010,X; bit 14 is the off-screen flag that the depth sort sets/clears, so a new actor starts flagged off-screen — reason inferred), computed entry point → $0000,X/$0002,X.

Player path (bit 15 of $10 set): Clears playerFlags $0088 (sprite priority | combat lock), then re-derives them from the spawn record's type byte: bit $02 sets the combat lock ($0008) and bit $04 sets the sprite-priority flag ($0080) — both bits are stripped from $0E afterwards. Non-combat scenes (towns, cutscene rooms) use type $02/$32; combat scenes use $00/$30. Parses direction sprite for initial facing, loads character form body table for spriteset, computes initial camera position (actor X +8 centering; camera = position − $80 clamped at 0; playerYPos = Y − $10), and initializes scroll registers.

Normal path: Sets default spriteset ($4000 bank $7E), calls UpdateActorAnimation, adds 8px X offset, then resolves stats table if present (index × 4 + base → statsPtr, first byte → currentHp).
InitActorPool:
Initialize both actor and thinker memory pools.

Actor pool:
- Free list stored at $0E00 as word-sized entries
- Long pointer $4E (word = $0E00) / $50 (bank byte = 0) addresses the next free entry; ActorPoolAllocator reads it with ($4E), AdvanceSceneDataAndFree writes back through [$4E]
- 84 actor slots, each $30 bytes, starting at $1000 ($1000, $1030, $1060, ... $1F90)
- Free list built by storing ascending slot addresses, terminated by $FFFF sentinel
- Zeroes the actor direct-page area ($1000–$1FBF), the extended fields at $7F1000–$7F1FBF (statsPtr, enemyNum, HP, iframeCounter... addressed as $7F0000+slot) and the callback block at $7F2000–$7F2FBF (onHitCallback... addressed as $7F1000+slot)

Thinker pool:
- Free list at $7E3000 (long pointer $52/$54, bank $7E)
- 16 thinker slots, each $10 bytes, starting at $0F00
- Free list built similarly with $FFFF sentinel
- Zeroes $0F00–$0FFF, $7F0E00–$7F0EFF and $7F3000–$7F30FF. The $7F0E00 range is one page below the $7F0F00 page that inventory_overlay saves as the thinkers' extended data; the role of $7F3000 is not traced

Scene $FF (the inventory screen, loaded over the running game by inventory_overlay) uses a simplified clear path that skips the $7F2000 callback block and the $7F3000 range — inventory_overlay does not back these up (inferred reason: the paused field actors' callbacks must survive the overlay).
InitCameraBounds:
Initialize camera boundary limits from map geometry or custom bounds.

Two paths based on $0652:

=== Normal path ($0652 = 0) ===
Copies mapBoundsX/Y directly to cameraBoundsX/Y and cameraLowerYBound. Zeroes cameraOffsetX/Y (no scroll offset from map origin).

=== Custom bounds path ($0652 ≠ 0) ===
Parses packed nibble format from $0652/$0653 into camera window parameters:
- $0652 low nibble → cameraOffsetX high byte (left edge, in 256-pixel units)
- $0652 high nibble → cameraOffsetY high byte (top edge)
- $0653 low nibble → cameraBoundsX high byte (right edge)
- $0653 high nibble → cameraBoundsY high byte (bottom edge), also stored to the high byte of cameraLowerYBound ($06DF)

Used for scenes with camera-restricted areas (e.g., boss arenas, cutscene frames).

=== Common finalization ===
Clears low bytes of cameraBoundsY and cameraLowerYBound. Zeroes $0652 (consumed). Applies visible height correction: cameraBoundsY += $0100 − visibleHeight ($06EC) (adjusts for the playable viewport height vs. the full map).
InitSplitFill: Fill the two COLDATA buffers ($7E8A00 and $7E8B00; the BGMODE buffers are not touched) with 76 words of $01FF, then a $0000 word (DBR = $7E). Not a 'fully open window' (no window register is involved): after the template's first 6 bytes the fill reads as a repeat-mode count byte $FF and data 01, FF, 01, FF, ..., the alternating COLDATA writes below the boundary row. The terminator word is never reached because the screen ends first. Called once at spawn.
InitSplitFillLoop: Fill loop: one $01FF word into each COLDATA buffer per pass, 76 passes.
InitThinkerFromSceneData:
Parse a thinker's binary scene data record from pointer $3E.

Record format (variable length):
- Byte 0: thinker type → stored to animScratch+2 ($7F0002,X)
- Bytes 1–2: code pointer → $42 (indirect)
- Byte 3: bank byte → $44

Advances $3E past the record. Then dereferences the code pointer to read its first word as animScratch2 ($7F000E,X = thinker filter flags), and stores the entry point (code + 2) and bank to thinker slot fields $0000 and $0002.
InteractionCollision_Exit: Common exit of the interaction pipeline: PLB, PLP, RTL.
InteractionCollision_FriendlyMode: Interaction pass for friendly NPCs: walks actorRenderList and skips every actor with any of $3540 set in $10, requires $0020 (friendly) to be set, then tests the probe box in $18–$1E against the actor's hitbox bytes (metasprite +4..+7) without horizontal mirroring. The first overlap calls ApplyInteractionDamage and returns, so at most one actor is processed per call.
InteractionDamage_NPCChat:
Handle NPC chat interaction — item giving and dialogue display.

Sets data bank to $81. Attempts to give the item referenced by chatPtr ($7F000A,X) to the player via GiveItemToPlayer. If inventory is full (carry set), shows the overflow message (dialog_item_full) and returns carry set.

If the item was given or chatPtr indicates dialogue: loads the chatPtr value. Values ≥ $81 are treated as dialogue script indices; values < $81 are item IDs shown in a dialogue frame. After interaction, converts the NPC actor to NpcDespawnStub (dead stub) by overwriting its entry point and zeroing the frame counter. Sets $0700 in flags to prevent re-interaction.
IrisCircleEffect:
HDMA iris/circle thinker entry point — odd-frame path writing to $7E8D00.

Saves and zeros the direct page register (PHD/TCD $0000) so all DP references use absolute addresses $00–$FF. Checks frame counter parity ($0036 bit 0): odd frames execute inline, even frames jump to IrisCircleEvenFrame.

=== COMPUTATION (16 bands, odd frame → $7E8D00) ===

Setup:
- WRMPYA = $60 (96) — constant multiplier for circle curve shaping
- $06 = $E0 — starting right window edge (224px, near right side of screen)
- $08 = $1F — running scanline accumulator (initial offset 31)
- $0E = ($0400 − $B6/2) × 2 — per-band step decrement (controls circle curvature)
- $00 = step × 16 — initial circle value (scaled up for fixed-point math)
- X = $1E — start from band 15, decrement to 0
- Write $E07F/$0000 sentinels at end of HDMA table

Per-band loop (loc_03A6FF):
1. 16×8 multiply via two 8×8 hardware ops: ($00 low × $60) → $02, ($01 high × $60) + carry → $03/$04
2. $04 = scanline count for this band (clamped to minimum 1)
3. Write scanline count to $7E8D00,X, right edge to $7E8D01,X
4. Accumulate scanline count into $08; BCS → overflow handler
5. Increment right edge ($06), subtract $0E from circle value ($00), DEX×2

=== HDMA CHANNEL SETUP (loc_03A755) ===

Restores DP (PLA/TCD), constructs A = $7E32 (bank $7E, register $32), Y = $7E8D00 + X offset, calls SetupHdmaChannel_Direct to configure the HDMA channel for next VBlank.

=== OVERFLOW HANDLER (loc_03A76F) ===

When accumulated scanlines exceed 255: subtracts the excess from the last band's scanline count and writes the final right edge without incrementing. Falls through to HDMA setup.
IrisCircleEvenFrame:
Even-frame path of the iris circle generator — identical algorithm writing to $7E8E00.

Mirrors IrisCircleEffect's odd-frame computation exactly, with all WRAM references offset from $7E8D00 to $7E8E00. The HDMA setup (loc_03A80F) passes Y = $7E8E00 + offset to SetupHdmaChannel_Direct. The overflow handler (loc_03A829) adjusts $7E8E00,X entries. Double-buffering prevents visual tearing: while one buffer drives the current frame's HDMA, the other is being regenerated for the next frame.
ItemHandlerJumpTable:
64-entry word table mapping item IDs $00–$3F to handler addresses.

Entries $00–$28 point to individual item handlers. Entries $29–$3F are unused and all point to UseItem_Unused (a single RTS). Items $1E–$23 (Hieroglyph Plates) all share UseItem_HieroglyphPlate.
ItemUseDispatch:
Entry point for inventory item usage.

Pushes ItemUseEpilogue−1 as an RTS-trick return address so each handler can simply RTS to reach the cleanup code. Reads the equipped slot index from inventoryEquippedIndex — if negative ($FFFF = nothing equipped), jumps to UseItem_None. Otherwise reads the item byte from inventorySlots, masks to a 6-bit item ID ($00–$3F), doubles it for a word-sized jump table index, consumes the use-item button ($0008 in joypadHeld) so holding it does not re-trigger the item, and dispatches through ItemHandlerJumpTable via indirect JMP.
ItemUseEpilogue: Post-handler cleanup for item use. Calls UpdateFrameDialogue to process one frame of dialogue/UI, consumes the use-item button ($0008 in joypadHeld) again, restores processor flags, and returns to the caller via RTL.
LoadGameState_Scene:
Load game state from an SRAM save slot, verifying data integrity first.

Slot number passed in A (masked to 0–3). Computes SRAM offset the same way as SaveGameState_Scene.

Calls ComputeSaveChecksum to recompute checksums over the SRAM data. Compares both the additive ($0018) and XOR ($001C) checksums against the stored values at $3063FC/$3063FE. If either mismatches, returns with carry SET (load failure — corrupted or empty slot).

On valid checksum: copies 508 bytes from SRAM $306200+offset back to event flags at $0A00. Returns with carry CLEAR (success).
LoadHudTilemap:
Load the heads-up display tilemap into the BG3 staging buffer ($7F:0200).

First checks hudDisableFlag ($09ED) bit 6 — if set, the HUD is suppressed (returns immediately). Scene command $02 (display_preset_table record byte +7 bit 7) sets or clears this bit for each scene.

Switches to 16-bit mode and sets data bank to current program bank (PHK/PLB) for direct access to HudTilemapData.

The data stream uses a simple format:
- Nonzero word: tile data — written directly to $7F0200,X (BG3 staging buffer)
- Zero word followed by nonzero word: skip command — the second word is a tile count to advance X by (×2 for word offset)
- Zero word followed by zero word: end of stream

After loading, sets displayModeFlags bit 0 ($0001) to signal that the BG3 staging buffer has pending data for the next VBlank transfer. The stream expands to 159 words (318 bytes), so it fits the first $0140 bytes that ClearBg3TilemapBuffer_PreserveHud preserves.
LoadMusicFromTransitionState:
Resolve a staged music ID and run the SPC block transfer.

Called once per main-loop pass from MainLoop, after UpdateHUD. Returns at once if musicTransitionState is zero or negative (no pending music change or already done).

For a positive ID it computes the music_pointer_array offset (ID − 1) × 3 (3-byte entries: address + bank) and loads the address into DP $46/$47 and into the shadow bytes $0687/$0688. It then enables NMI and joypad, calls SpcBlockTransfer (blocking; the NMI calls UpdateFrameFull every frame while musicTransitionState is positive), switches to DisableNmiKeepJoypad (NMITIMEN = $01: NMI off, joypad auto-read on; the main loop turns NMI on again at the end of the pass) and stores $FFFF into musicTransitionState to release the waiting SpcTransferMusicData thinker.
LoadPlayerGraphics:
Load player character sprite graphics to VRAM.

Checks the current scene against a skip list — scenes $F7, $FE, $8C don't load player graphics (no visible player character).

For normal scenes:
1. Sets VMADDL to $4200 and DMA transfers $1C00 bytes (7168 bytes = 224 4bpp tiles) from gfx_000000 to VRAM. This is the main player character spriteset.

2. If playerFlags bit 3 ($08, combat lock — non-combat scene) is set: loads $0800 bytes (2048 bytes = 64 tiles) of FX graphics from misc_fx_1CD580 to VRAM $4400, overwriting the part of the main spriteset just uploaded at byte offset $0400 (tiles 32–95). Combat-allowed scenes skip this; their ability tiles are uploaded on demand by the ability VRAM DMA loaders.

3. If scene is $E8 (Dark Gaia boss fight) and playerFlags bit 3 is NOT set: loads $0600 bytes (1536 bytes = 48 tiles) of alternative FX graphics from misc_fx_1CCA80 to VRAM $4400. These are the ranged projectile tiles used during the final boss.

All transfers go through DmaWordToVram (extracted/system/engine/DmaWordToVram.asm); the caller presets VMADDL, X = source address, A = source bank, Y = byte count.
LoadScenePalettes:
Load standard scene palettes with character-form-specific overrides.

Operates in 16-bit mode. Skip rules, by sceneCurrent:
- Scene $F7 (intro sequence): skip all palette loading
- Scenes $F0, $FD, $FF (title screen): load only the HUD/UI palette — skip the game palette and the non-combat palette

Sequence:
1. (all scenes except $F7) COP CopyPalette fx_palette_198040: source=@198040, start=1, dest=1, count=23. This is the standard HUD/UI palette.
2. (all scenes except $F0, $FD, $FF) COP CopyPalette fx_palette_198020: start=0, dest=$90, count=16. This is the standard game palette.
3. If playerFlags bit 3 ($0008, combat lock — non-combat scene): copies 32 bytes (16 colors) from fx_palette_198000 to $7F:0B40 (CGRAM mirror color $A0, 512-byte mirror at $7F0A00) with the block-move helper at $0402. That helper is a WRAM routine set up by wram-init as PHB / MVN / PLB / RTS; $0404 and $0405 are the MVN destination and source banks (A = byte count − 1; the destination bank is assumed to be $7F, left there by earlier setup).
loc_03EFA2: Slot scan for regular items: Y = 0 to 15, the first slot holding 0 is used.
loc_03EFAA: Slot occupied: next slot; after 16 slots the inventory is full.
loc_03EFB3: Special item: effect index := id - $80, then a DEC chain tests 0 (HP), 1 (STR), 2 (DEF), 3 to 5 (gems); anything else falls into the heal code that follows.
loc_03EFC1: Effect index 3 and above: gems (3, 4, 5) or the heal.
loc_03EFF3: Adds the amount in A to gemCount, clamps at 999 and plays SFX $22.
loc_03F004: Stores gemCount, plays SFX $22 and returns through GiveItem_Success.
loc_03F00C: HP Max Up (item $80): display-filter clear, SFX $25, max HP + 1 with the $7F reset, hpToHeal := new max - HP, Y = 0.
loc_03F023: Stores the new max HP and sets hpToHeal.
loc_03F032: STR Up (item $81): display-filter clear, SFX $25, STR + 1 with the $7F reset, Y = 0.
loc_03F093: Slot scan for RemoveItemFromInventory: compares each slot with the id in A.
loc_03F0A0: Match: zero the slot, then unequip (type 0, index $FFFF).
LookupMapName: Search world_map_scene_names (3-byte entries: scene id, name pointer) for the scene id in $0000. Found: Y := name pointer. Not found: Y is returned unchanged (the table has no terminator, see world_map_scene_names). Called with the source scene $0D6F at the start and the destination $0D6E at the end.
LookupMapNameFound: Match: Y := the name pointer at world_map_scene_names + 1 + X, restore DBR / X / P and return.
LookupMapNameLoop: Search loop of LookupMapName: compare the scene id of entry X with $0000; a zero id byte ends the search (miss), a match goes to LookupMapNameFound, otherwise X advances by 3.
LookupMapNameMiss: Zero id byte reached (no match): restore DBR / X / P and return with Y unchanged.
MenuSelection_Confirm: A/Start branch of the poll loop: saves and restores $0A/$0C around the redraw, plays SFX $11, clears the blink counter ($0994), redraws the cursor solid, turns the 0-based selection into a 1-based result and falls into MenuSelection_Return.
MenuSelection_Down:
Handle Down input in menu selection.

Extracts grid dimensions from the packed stack parameter (high nibble = total, low nibble = columns). Increments the selection index. If it exceeds the column count (entering the second page), wraps or caps to the total count. Plays navigation sound and returns to the poll loop.
MenuSelection_LeftRight:
Handle L/R input for column-based menu navigation.

Adds or subtracts the column count to/from the current selection. Clamps to grid bounds. If the result crosses a page boundary, plays the navigation sound; otherwise returns silently to the poll loop.
MenuSelection_Return: Shared exit of MenuSelectionHandler: one-frame wait, clears the blink counter and saved cursor tiles, restores the registers and returns carry set with the 1-based selection (0 = cancelled).
MenuSelection_Up: Up branch of MenuSelection_PollLoop: plays SFX $10, unpacks the grid position from the stack byte, decrements the selection (wrapping through MenuSelection_UpWrap when it goes below zero) and returns to the poll loop.
MenuSelection_UpWrap: Reached when Up takes the selection below zero: wraps to the last item (the last index of the column, or of the second column) and returns to the poll loop.
MenuSelectionHandler:
General-purpose menu selection handler for dialogue choices.

Entry: JSL. Stack parameter at SP+3 encodes the menu grid: high nibble = total item count (rows × columns), low nibble = items per row (column count). SP+1 = initial selection index. SP+5 = starting row offset.

Saves DP and sets it to 0. Initializes cursor blink counter ($0994) to 0.

The main loop (MenuSelection_PollLoop) draws the cursor, waits one frame, and checks joypad input:
- Up ($0800): Decrement index with row-aware wrapping
- Down ($0400): Increment index with row-aware wrapping
- L/R ($0300): Add/subtract column count for page navigation
- A/Start ($8080): Confirm — play sound #11, restore tiles under cursor, increment selection by 1, return carry set
- B ($4000): Cancel — call ReadMenuSelection to restore tiles, return A = 0, carry set

All navigation plays sound #10 and resets cursor blink. Returns: A = 1-based selection index (0 = cancelled), carry set.
Mode7AltQ1_PosCosPosSin:
Unused quadrant 1 (+cos, +sin) — reverse-fill scanline loop.

Per-scanline: hardware divide |cos| ÷ scale → $7E7100,X (M7A), |sin| ÷ scale → $7E7900,X (M7B), negate → $7E8100,X (M7C). DEX×2 per iteration from $01C0 down to 0. Subtracts $04 from accumulator $01 each scanline. On borrow (BCC → DEC $03), continues without halving. Quadrants 2–4 follow the same pattern with appropriate sign inversions and swapped table destinations.
Mode7CosNegative: cos < 0: negate cos, re-read sin and choose the third or fourth quadrant routine.
Mode7CosNegSinNegative: cos < 0 and sin < 0: negate sin and enter the fourth quadrant routine.
Mode7FillTableLoop: Fill loop: one entry per scanline in all three tables (count byte 1, data bytes left 0), 224 times, then $00 terminators.
Mode7PerspectiveAlt:
Unused Mode 7 perspective entry point — HDMA table init and per-frame matrix computation.

Phase 1 — Header initialization: sets up 3-entry indirect HDMA headers for all three tables. Each header has three $F0 (240 scanline) count bytes at offsets 0/3/6, with 16-bit WRAM data addresses pointing into the table data regions:
- Table A ($7E7000): headers → $7100/$71E0 (M7A data)
- Table B ($7E7800): headers → $7900/$79E0 (M7B data)
- Table C ($7E8000): headers → $8100/$81E0 (M7C data)

Yields via SetEntryHere after header setup.

Phase 2 — Per-frame computation: loads scale ($B8 → $02), rotation ($B6 → $04), perspective angle ($BC). Sine/cosine lookup from sine_table_16bit/01C695 with 4-quadrant dispatch. Starts from X=$01C0 and works downward. Pushes QueueMode7HdmaAlt−1 as RTS-trick return. Does NOT call NormalizeDivisor — divisor is used as-is.

Key difference from active version: subtracts rotation increment (SEC/SBC $04 → $01) instead of adding, and uses BCC/DEC for underflow handling.
Mode7PerspectiveInit: Thinker entry for scene $FE only. M7SEL := $80; $7F0B22 and $7F0B24 := $FFFF; Mode 7 centre := world-map start position; camera := centre - ($80, $70) with the bit 15 scroll-override flag; $B6 := 0, $BC := 0, $B8 := $0400. Falls through into Mode7PerspectiveUpdate.
Mode7PerspectiveUpdate:
Table fill (first tick only) followed by the per-frame matrix computation. Entered by fall-through from Init (scene $FE) or directly as the SpawnThinker target of the prologue, Sky Garden crash and Angkor Wat vision scripts. COP SetEntryHere separates the one-time fill from the per-frame part.
Per frame: scratch $02 := $B8 (divisor), $04 := $B6 (increment), index Y := ($BC AND $1FF) x 2, then cos and sin from the 16-bit tables, absolute values in $18 and $1C, jump to the matching quadrant routine with QueueMode7HdmaTables-1 on the stack.
Mode7Q1Overflow: Quadrant 1 overflow: add the carry to the divisor high byte, halve |cos|, |sin|, the divisor word and the increment, and continue the loop.
Mode7Q1Scanline: Scanline loop of quadrant 1: two divides, three table writes, divisor accumulation.
Mode7Quadrant_NegCosPosSin: Quadrant 3 (-cos, +sin). A := 0 - cos/div, B := sin/div, C := -(sin/div). Uses 4 NOPs because the LDA #0 / SEC / SBC read delays the RDDIVL access.
Mode7Quadrant_PosCosNegSin: Quadrant 2 (+cos, -sin). Same as quadrant 1 but the sin quotient goes to table C unchanged and its negation to table B, so B = sin/div (negative) and C = -sin/div (positive).
Mode7Quadrant_PosCosPosSin: Quadrant 1 (+cos, +sin). NormalizeDivisor, then 224 scanlines: A := cos/div, B := sin/div, C := -(sin/div), divisor += $B6/256. Carry out of the accumulator halves everything (Mode7Q1Overflow).
Mode7SinNegative: cos >= 0 and sin < 0: negate sin and enter the second quadrant routine.
NormalizeDivisor: Shift the divisor word, |cos|, |sin| and the increment right together until the divisor high byte is zero, so the divisor fits the 8-bit WRDIVB register. The ratios, and therefore the quotients, are unchanged.
NormalizeDivisorShift: Shift step of NormalizeDivisor: A = divisor >> 1, then $18, $1C and $04 shifted too, and test again.
OamHiTableMasks:
8-byte lookup table for OAM high-table bit packing.

Provides pre-computed mask pairs used to finalize partial hi-table bytes when the compose buffer sprite count doesn't align to a 4-sprite boundary. Indexed by ($00DA LSR AND $06) — the number of leftover sprites mod 4, doubled for word access.
PlayerAttackHitTest:
Test the player's attack hitbox against all enemies and apply damage on hit.

Constructs the player's attack AABB from the metasprite header: $0000/$0001 are signed X/Y offsets (sign-extended from 8 bits via ORA #$FF00), $0002/$0003 are unsigned widths (×16 via ASL ×4). The result is stored in DP $00–$06 as the bounding box.

Then iterates all actors in the render list, skipping those with exclusion flags ($36F0). For each candidate, reads the actor's hitbox fields ($0020–$0023) as signed offsets from position, computes the AABB, and tests overlap against the player's box.

On hit: applies damage = chainDamage/2 + 1. chainDamage ($7F101E,X) accumulates across consecutive hits within the same attack sequence. Enemy HP = max(0, HP − damage). If HP reaches 0: checks for onDeathCallback or defaults to StandardEnemyDefeatHandler. If alive: spawns HitStaggerMain for knockback, computes knockback direction, assigns iframeCounter: $0011 (positive = hit-stun: non-player actors skip their tick, the player's tick still runs), or $FFEF (negative = recovery: counts up toward zero, the tick still runs) when $12 bit 0 ($0001) is set.

Damage digits are formatted via FormatDamageDigits and spawned as SpawnDamageNumberEffect floating numbers (spawn flags $2F00). Enemy HP is written to the HUD display registers.
PlayerAttackHitTest_End: Tail of PlayerAttackHitTest: resets the direct page to 0 (TCD) and returns with RTS.
PlayerSprite_OffScreen:
Handle player sprite being off-screen during decomposition.

Sets bit 2 ($0004) in playerFlags (sprite-redraw request: CheckPlayerSpriteCache bypasses its cache while it is set) and bit 3 ($0008) in displayModeFlags (player tile DMA pending). Writes $E080 to the current OAM slot to scrub it, without advancing Y, then continues with the remaining sub-sprites. Reached from the Y check before the sub-sprite's tile is queued, and from the X check after it was queued.
ProcessDodgeCallbacks:
Trigger dodge callbacks when the attack/action button ($0080 bit of joypadCurrent) is pressed.

Iterates the actor render list ($0C00). For each actor without exclusion flags ($D460 = death|orb|COP|overlay|pause bits), checks if onDodgeCallback ($7F1002,X) is set. If so, overwrites the actor's entry point ($0000,X) with the callback address and clears the callback to prevent re-trigger.

This allows actors to react to the player's dodge/attack button press — used by interactive objects and enemy dodge behaviors.
QueueMode7HdmaAlt:
RTS-trick return target — queues 4 HDMA transfers via COP QueueHdma.

Identical register targets to the active version ($1B–$1E for M7A–M7D), but uses QueueHdma instead of QueueHdmaDirect. Table A ($7E7000) is reused for both M7A ($1B) and M7D ($1E).
QueueMode7HdmaTables: RTS-trick return target. Restores D and the thinker slot, then queues four direct-table HDMA transfers: table A to M7A ($211B), B to M7B ($211C), C to M7C ($211D) and A again to M7D ($211E). Ends with RTL back to the thinker loop.
QueueSplitTables: Queue the two tables built this frame with COP QueueHdmaDirect: even frames $7E8800 -> BGMODE ($2105) and $7E8A00 -> COLDATA ($2132); odd frames $7E8900 and $7E8B00 to the same registers. Each COP takes a direct-table HDMA channel for the next frame.
RadarBorderAnimate:
Animate the radar border color on odd frames (JSR from GlobalInputHandler's display loop).

Returns at once when bit 0 of frameCounter ($0036) is clear. Otherwise it increments the animation index stored in the caller's stack word ($03,S), wraps it at 29, and writes RadarBorderColorTable[index] to $7F0A24 (cgramPalette color 18). The values are BGR555 colors, not tilemap words, so the border pulses through a blue → yellow → blue palette cycle.
RadarBorderColorTable:
29 BGR555 colors for the radar border animation.

RadarBorderAnimate writes one entry per odd frame to cgramPalette color 18 ($7F0A24). Decoded values run from blue ($5C82: R2 G4 B23) through yellow ($4BBF: R31 G29 B18) and back to blue ($58E5).
RadarPlotActors:
Walk the actor list (head $56, next at $0006,X) and plot dots by extendedFlags.

Bit 8 ($0100) routes to RadarPlotFriendlyActor, which plots the stat-bearing enemies, and bit 9 ($0200) to RadarPlotEnemyActor, which plots the Dark Space portals. Bit 8 is set by InitActorFromSceneData (actor_execution) for actors spawned with combat stats and an enemy number (they are counted in enemiesRemaining), so that dot marks the stat-bearing enemies still in the actor list. Bit 9 is set only by dark_space.asm (COP OrExtraFlags #$0200 in DarkSpacePortalInit), so that dot marks a Dark Space portal. Bit 8 is tested first, so an actor with both bits gets the enemy dot. Actors with neither bit are not plotted.
RadarPlotEnemyActor:
Plot one bit-9 actor (a Dark Space portal) as dot tile word $280D.

Same cell math as RadarPlotFriendlyActor, after one extra test against cameraOffsetX/Y..cameraBoundsX/Y. Those four words are the scene's scroll limits, not the current view, so the extra test only rejects positions outside the scene. $280D is tile $00D with palette 2 (not palette 0).
RadarPlotFriendlyActor:
Plot one bit-8 actor (a stat-bearing enemy) as the enemy dot, tile word $2AE7.

Skips actors whose pixel position ($0014,X/$0016,X) is outside the viewport ($0018/$001A × $001C/$001E). Cell offset: column = ((x − left) >> 5) AND $FFFE, row = (y − top) AND $FFC0, plus $0216, written into $7F0200. $2AE7 is tile $2E7 with palette 2 and is also the legend icon beside the remaining-enemy count. Always returns with carry set.
RadarPlotSceneMarkers:
Plot the unopened treasure chests of the current scene and count them in BCD (scratch $0002).

sceneTableIndex ($0646) is a byte index into the pointer list at the head of scene_chest_table; the word found there is the address of this scene's record list. Each 4-byte record: byte 0 = X tile (bit 7 set = end of list), byte 1 = Y tile of the chest's bottom row, byte 2 = contents (0 = flag only), byte 3 = event flag (AND $7F; bit 7 = fanfare). A set event flag (TestEventFlag_0200) means the chest is already opened, so it is skipped and not counted.

Every unopened chest is counted, whether or not it lies inside the viewport. Those inside get the tile $2EE6 written at the cell offset (+$0216 radar interior base into $7F0200).
RadarScreenSetup:
Build the radar screen (JSR from GlobalInputHandler when Start opens the map).

Waits for any pending adhoc VRAM DMA, queues the icon graphics DMA (512 bytes to VRAM $7700) and waits for it, clears the staging buffer, block-copies the radar layout, computes the viewport and then plots chests, actors, legend counts and the optional clear-reward frame. See the file header for the full pipeline and cell geometry.

Reward block: when flag $0300 + sceneCurrent is clear and enemy_clear_reward_table[scene] is non-zero it draws a 4×4-cell frame (corner tile $2EE1 with H/V flips, edges $2EE2/$2EE3 with flips) around a 2×2 icon of sequential tiles $32E8–$32EB and runs the BG3 label script. The table value (1=HP, 2=STR, 3=DEF per boss_clear_reward_handler) is only tested for non-zero here; what the icon shows is unverified.
ReadMenuSelection:
Restore tiles under the menu cursor and convert position to OAM data.

Restores the saved tiles ($0990/$0992) to their original VRAM buffer positions. Converts the tile values to OAM-compatible format: strips palette/priority bits (AND $03FF), shifts left 3 (ASL ×3), and OR's with $6000 for the OAM priority. Writes to $090E/$0910 for sprite overlay use. Clears the saved tile state.
RemoveEquippedItem:
Remove the currently equipped item from inventory.

Reads inventoryEquippedIndex into Y, switches to 8-bit accumulator mode, and writes $00 to the item slot byte at inventorySlots,Y. Returns to 16-bit mode, sets inventoryEquippedType to $0000 and inventoryEquippedIndex to $FFFF (−1 = no selection). Called by item handlers that consume the equipped item via JSR rather than the COP RemoveItem command.
RemoveItemFromInventory:
Remove an item from inventory by ID.

Searches all 16 inventorySlots for the item ID in A. If found: zeroes the slot, resets inventoryEquippedType to 0 and inventoryEquippedIndex to $FFFF (nothing equipped). If not found: returns silently.
RenderComposeBuffer:
Render pre-composed sprites from the compose buffer ($7F3100) into OAM.

Two rendering modes based on layerPriorityFlag bit 12 ($1000):

Normal mode (bit clear): Iterates the compose buffer (6 bytes per entry). For each entry, subtracts scroll offsets to convert to screen coordinates, bounds-checks Y (< $F0) and X (< $110), and writes to OAM low table ($0422,Y) with hi-table bit packing. Entries are consumed in groups of 6 bytes (X += 6), OAM advances by 4 bytes (Y += 4).

Layer priority mode (bit set): Block-copies compose buffer data directly to OAM via MVN $00,$7F. Copies min($00DA, $0200) bytes from $7F0600 to $0422 ($00DA is a byte count, 4 per sprite — pr_text_placement_calc builds the entries and doubles its sprite count twice). Then computes the hi-table byte count ($00DA >> 4), fills those bytes with $AA (every sprite large-size, X bit 8 clear) and sets the rolling register for the leftover sprites from OamHiTableMasks. Y is left at $00DA, so actor sprites follow the copied block. No setter for bit 12 of layerPriorityFlag was found in the extracted code, so what triggers this mode is unconfirmed.
ResetHdmaState:
Reset the HDMA channel allocation state for fresh channel assignment (every frame routine calls this once per frame before the type-B/D thinkers).

If $6C is negative (bit 7 set) the reset is skipped. $6C is a one-shot lock: scene_lifecycle's wave transition arms it ($FF) right after its own explicit reset so that the ApplyScrollWaveEffect → UpdateFrameDialogue call does not wipe the HDMA channels the wave just bound.

Otherwise clears the HDMA enable mask ($66 = 0), resets the next channel bit to channel 1 ($68 = $02) and the DMA register block offset to channel 1 ($6A = $10). SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect/Direct consume these three bytes.

Always clears the lock ($6C = 0) on exit, so the lock covers exactly one call.
RouteAnimationEngine: Interpreter for the route bytes of world_map_route_table[$0D5A]. A step is four bytes: move_chain_table indices for X ($CA), Y ($CC) and rotation ($BC), then a tick count n (the step runs n + 1 ticks). Index 0 is null (that axis stands still). $FF ends the route, $FE calls a subroutine (2-byte target, one level). Each tick adds the next delta of each active axis and sets cameraTargetX/Y = centre - ($80, $70). The delta chains come from move_chain_table (constants +-1.. and half-speed alternations).
RouteAxisRotation: Y axis done or absent: add the rotation delta chain $1C to the rotation index $BC.
RouteAxisY: X axis done or absent (null chain pointer): handle the Y axis in the same way (chain pointer $1A, world Y $00CC, cameraTargetY = Y - $70).
RouteCountTick: End of the tick: decrement the remaining tick count; while it is still non-negative the actor yields (RTL).
RouteDeltaTables: Normal step: byte 0 (the X chain index, already read) and bytes 1 and 2 (the Y and rotation chain indices) select the delta chains in move_chain_table ($18, $1A, $1C), and byte 3, the tick count n, is stored in $24. SetEntryHere only saves the re-entry point (it does not yield); the actor adds the next delta of each active axis and yields at the RTL in RouteCountTick, so the step applies its deltas n + 1 times, once per tick.
RouteEndHandler: Route byte $FF. A pending subroutine return (nonzero $0D5C) continues the caller. A true end: clear route and choice ids (the dots notice and die), show the destination name (scene $0D6E) for 60 ticks (WaitByte #3B), then lower $B6 by $10 per frame until it would go negative (the map is flat again; Start skips to the scene change). Landing: $B6 := 0, transition speeds gfxCacheIdxB := $0406, restore the deferred scene change, clear the state block, and from then on add the TickGravity delta to $B8 every frame (zoom-in dive) until the scene changes.
RouteEndLanding: Landing: perspective gone, restore the deferred scene change and start the zoom-in dive while the scene exit runs.
RouteNextStep: The count went negative: the step is complete, continue with the next one at RouteStepLoop.
RouteNotEnd: The step byte is not $FF: advance past it; $FE calls a subroutine (RouteSubroutineCall), anything else is the X delta index of a normal step.
RouteStepLoop: Read the next step: $FF -> RouteEndHandler, $FE -> RouteSubroutineCall, otherwise load the three delta chain pointers and the tick count and start the step.
RouteSubroutineCall: Route byte $FE: remember the address after the 2-byte target in $0D5C and continue at the target. One nesting level only; a second $FE would overwrite $0D5C. No shipped route uses it: no step in world_map_route_table starts with $FE (every route is 4n step bytes plus a hidden $FF end byte).
RouteTrulyEnded: True end of the route (no subroutine return pending).
RunActors_CopScriptPostTick:
Post-tick handler for actors that just returned from COP script execution.

Checks whether bit 13 ($2000) of $10 is still set (the script may have cleared it). If cleared, falls into the normal PostTick. If still set, checks secondary flags ($12) bit 3 ($0008) — a script-driven actor only gets movement when that bit requests it. If set, performs PostTick; if clear, skips directly to the next actor.
RunActors_CutsceneOnly:
Cutscene-only actor execution — processes only cutscene-flagged actors.

Active during cutscene playback. Clears bit 2 of $10 for every actor (not just processed ones). Only dispatches COP scripts for actors with bit 11 ($0800) set — the cutscene-active flag. Actors without this flag skip directly to the next-actor link.

No iframe management is performed in this mode.
RunActors_CutsceneOnly_CopPostTick: Post-tick entry for script-driven actors in the cutscene pass: movement only when $12 bit 3 is set.
RunActors_CutsceneOnly_PostTick: Post-tick of the cutscene pass: movement via ApplyMovementWithCollision ($10 bit 3 set) or ApplyMovement; the bit-2 clear already happened at the top of the actor loop. Ends at $06 = 0.
RunActors_DisplayFiltered:
Display-filtered actor execution — processes only display-active actors.

Active when displayModeFlags bit 7 ($0080) is set. Iterates the actor linked list but only processes actors where bit 12 ($1000) is set in either primary flags ($10) or secondary flags ($12). Actors without this flag are skipped entirely (no COP dispatch, no movement).

Otherwise identical lifecycle to RunActors_Normal: iframe management, COP script dispatch, collision/simple movement selection.
RunActors_DisplayFiltered_CopPostTick: Post-tick entry for script-driven actors ($10 bit 13): they skip the movement step unless $12 bit 3 (movement request) is set; all others take RunActors_DisplayFiltered_PostTick.
RunActors_DisplayFiltered_Exit: Common exit of the display-filtered pass: PLD, PLP, RTL.
RunActors_DisplayFiltered_PostTick: Post-tick of the display-filtered pass: clears $10 bit 2 (per-frame solid-contact flag), then moves the actor with ApplyMovementWithCollision when $10 bit 3 is set, else plain ApplyMovement. Loops to the next actor while $06 is non-zero, otherwise falls into _Exit.
RunActors_Normal:
Standard actor execution loop — primary gameplay processing mode.

Entry point for actor updates during normal gameplay. Saves processor state (PHP/PHD), switches to 16-bit mode, then checks game state flags to determine processing mode:
- playerFlags bit 3 ($0008): Combat lock — clears the attack button ($0080) from joypadCurrent
- playerFlags bit 4 ($0010): Terrain shake (landing of the Freedan ledge-jump drop attack) — redirects to RunActors_PauseFiltered
- displayModeFlags bit 7 ($0080): Display filter — redirects to RunActors_DisplayFiltered

If no filter is active, processes the actor linked list starting from $56. For each actor:
1. Sets DP and X to the actor's slot address (TCD/TAX)
2. If bit 13 ($2000) of $10 is set: decrements the wait counter ($08) and, once it is negative, dispatches the script and continues at RunActors_CopScriptPostTick (no iframe handling on this path)
3. Otherwise, if bit 7 ($0080) is set, manages the iframe counter ($7F0028,X): positive = hit-stun (DEC; non-player actors skip the rest of their tick), negative = recovery (INC toward zero, tick continues), zero clears $0080
4. Decrements the wait counter ($08) and, once it is negative, dispatches the script via the RTL indirect call trick
5. Post-tick: clears bit 2 of $10, then applies movement (collision-aware if bit 3 ($0008) of $10 is set, simple otherwise)
6. Follows $06 link to next actor

The COP dispatch pattern (PHK/PEA/SEP/LDA/PHA/REP/LDA/DEC/PHA/RTL) constructs a 3-byte target address and 3-byte return address on the stack. RTL pops and jumps to the target; when the actor script returns via RTL, execution resumes at the PostTick handler.
RunActors_OverlayOnly:
Overlay-only actor execution — processes overlay actors with special display handling.

First checks displayModeFlags bit 7 ($0080) — if set, redirects entirely to RunActors_DisplayFiltered (display filter takes precedence over overlay).

Otherwise, only processes actors with bit 12 ($1000) set in secondary flags ($12). Unlike other modes, the PostTick always uses simple ApplyMovement (no tile collision check), since overlay actors typically don't interact with terrain.
RunActors_OverlayOnly_CopPostTick: Post-tick entry for script-driven actors in the overlay pass: movement only when $12 bit 3 is set.
RunActors_OverlayOnly_PostTick: Post-tick of the overlay pass: always the plain ApplyMovement (no tile collision), then the next actor while $06 is non-zero.
RunActors_PauseFiltered:
Pause-filtered actor execution — processes only pause-immune actors.

Active when playerFlags bit 4 ($0010) is set (terrain shake: the landing of the Freedan ledge-jump drop attack freezes the world). Two paths to qualify:
1. Secondary flags ($12) bits 12|2 ($1004) set — secondary pause immunity
2. Primary flags ($10) bits 12|10 ($1400) set — primary pause immunity

Actors failing both checks go to an iframe-only handler (loc_03CCCD) that still counts down iframe timers but skips COP dispatch entirely. This ensures invincibility timers don't freeze during pause.

Pause-immune actors get full script dispatch and collision movement, allowing cutscene actors, UI elements, and certain effects to continue running during pause.

Quirk: when an actor qualifies through the $12 test, A still holds $12 (it is not reloaded as DisplayFiltered does), so the following bit-13 and iframe ($0080) tests read the $12 word instead of $10 on that path. Both paths use the same code afterwards.
RunActors_PauseFiltered_CopPostTick: Post-tick entry for script-driven actors in the pause-filtered pass: movement only when $12 bit 3 is set, otherwise straight to the loop tail.
RunActors_PauseFiltered_Exit: Exit of the pause-filtered pass (PLD, PLP, RTL). The code after the RTL (loc_03CCCD) is the iframe-only tail for non-immune paused actors: a positive iframeCounter is decremented, a negative one incremented toward zero, and when it reaches zero $10 bit 7 ($0080) is cleared, so recovery keeps ticking while the world is paused.
RunActors_PauseFiltered_PostTick: Post-tick of the pause-filtered pass: same bit-2 clear and movement choice as the other passes, then ends the pass when $06 is zero or re-enters the list body for the next actor.
RunActors_PostTick:
Post-tick handler shared by Normal and CopScriptPostTick paths.

Clears bit 2 ($0004) of $10 — the per-frame solid-contact flag (set by tile_collision_physics BlockH/BlockV) is reset before movement. Then checks bit 3 ($0008 of $10): if set, calls ApplyMovementWithCollision for full tile collision-aware movement; otherwise calls ApplyMovement for simple delta application. (Measured: with bit 3 cleared on the player, Will walks through a wall that stops him otherwise; the bit selects collision-aware movement and is not a hit flag.)

After movement, reads $06 (next actor link). If nonzero, loops back to process the next actor. If zero (end of list), restores DP/flags via PLD/PLP/RTL.
RunCombatCollision:
Entry point for the per-frame combat collision system.

Saves processor state and data bank. Zeroes enemyHpPending ($09EA) to clear any stale HP display request. Loads the player actor slot from $09AA and checks bit 6 ($0040) of the player's flags — if set (orb/special state), jumps directly to CombatCollision_Exit (no combat during orb). Otherwise falls through to CombatCollision_EnemyLoop.
RunInteractionCollision:
Player-vs-NPC/object interaction collision system.

Constructs a player interaction bounding box: X ± 4px from position, Y range from (Y−14) to (Y−4). This smaller box is centered higher than the combat hitbox, matching the player's interaction hotspot.

Checks the player actor's flags ($10, not playerFlags): $2040 (COP mode or orb) → exit immediately. $0280 (iframe/stagger or climb) → InteractionCollision_FriendlyMode (restricted to friendly NPCs).

Normal mode: iterates render list, skipping $35C0 flagged actors. For each candidate: sets data bank to actor's sprite bank, reads metasprite hitbox, accounts for H-mirror, and tests AABB overlap. On overlap: checks extendedFlags $0010 for collision callback. If callback exists, dispatches it; otherwise sets actor to smooth_follow_child default handler. Then calls ApplyInteractionDamage.

FriendlyMode: only tests actors with $0020 flag (friendly). Simplified hitbox test without H-mirror path. Single-hit return (first overlap triggers interaction and exits).
RunThinkers_General:
Execute thinkers with animScratch2 ($7F000E,X) bit 2 ($0004) CLEAR (called by MainLoop after the VBlank sync, and by the scene-start sequence).

Iterates the thinker linked list from $5A with D = X = slot. For each thinker: bit 2 set → next. Otherwise DEC $08 / BPL → next while the wait counter was positive; when it was 0 the script runs and $08 is cleared. There is no bit-11 test here.

Typical general thinkers: palette cyclers (ambient_palette_cycler), boot-logo palettes, color-add effects.
RunThinkers_General_Light:
Execute thinkers with animScratch2 bit 11 ($0800) SET and bit 2 ($0004) CLEAR.

Called by UpdateFrameDialogue, UpdateFrameRender and UpdateFrameFull after their VBlank sync. It is RunThinkers_General plus a bit-11 requirement: the 59 scene thinker-defs all carry bit 11 and run here, but a runtime-spawned thinker without bit 11 is paused whenever one of these lighter frame routines runs.
RunThinkers_Hdma:
Execute thinkers with animScratch2 ($7F000E,X) bit 2 ($0004) SET — the complement of RunThinkers_General.

MainLoop and the scene-start sequence call it right after ResetHdmaState, so thinkers that bind HDMA channels (comet_lair_hdma_*, angel_tunnel_window_dma, dao_sine_hdma_slow, ...) get fresh channels every frame. Same wait-counter dispatch as RunThinkers_General.
RunThinkers_Hdma_Light:
Execute thinkers with BOTH animScratch2 bits 11 ($0800) AND 2 ($0004) SET.

Uses AND #$0804 / CMP #$0804 to verify both bits. Called by UpdateFrameDialogue, UpdateFrameRender and UpdateFrameFull after ResetHdmaState and before the VBlank sync — it is RunThinkers_Hdma's counterpart in the lighter frame routines: scene thinkers (all with bit 11) run here, runtime-spawned thinkers only if they carry bit 11.
SaveGameState_Scene:
Save current game state (WRAM $0A00–$0BFB plus the scene ID) to an SRAM save slot.

Slot number passed in A (masked to 0–3). Computes the SRAM offset as (slot & 3) × 512 via XBA + ASL.

First stores the current scene number (sceneCurrent → $0B06) so it is part of the saved data. Then copies 508 bytes ($01FC) from $0A00 to SRAM at $306200 + offset.

Calls ComputeSaveChecksum and stores the additive checksum at $3063FC and the XOR checksum at $3063FE (+ slot offset). Both are verified on load.
ScanPartyArray: Party scan: Y steps through $0D62, $0D64, ... and stops at the first empty slot or at Y = $0C. Y - 2 is then 2 x the number of companions.
ScreenEnterTransition:
Visual enter transition effect dispatcher — selects from 4 effect types.

Dispatches on the high byte of gfxCacheIdxA ($0649):

- Type 0 (Graduated fade-in): Brightness ramps from 1 up to $0F. $064B (high byte of gfxCacheIdxB) controls the frame delay between steps, the enter-side counterpart of the exit speed byte $064A. Each step writes to INIDISP and increments until reaching full brightness ($10 comparison catches the >= $0F case).

- Type 1 (Instant display): Single UpdateFrameDialogue, then sets INIDISP to $0F. Fastest enter.

- Type 2 (Mosaic dissolve-in): Brightness ramps from 0 up to $0F while MOSAIC register decreases (pixel size shrinks from maximum to 1:1). Computed as (15 − brightness) << 4 | 3. The reverse of exit type 2 — large mosaic pixels dissolve into the sharp final image.

- Type 3 (Wave scroll enter): Initializes the HDMA sine wave with amplitude $80 ($006E) and spatial frequency 6 ($0070). The amplitude is decremented each pass (the loop ends when it reaches 0), so the wave shrinks as the screen fades in. Brightness ramps up as the wave settles, clamped at $0F. After the amplitude reaches 0, a wind-down loop steps brightness up to $0F with $064B-frame delays between steps.

All types call UpdateFrameDialogue per frame for audio/display sync.
ScreenExitTransition:
Visual exit transition effect dispatcher — selects from 5 effect types.

Dispatches on the low byte of gfxCacheIdxA ($0648):

- Type 0 (Graduated fade): Brightness ramps from $0F down to 0 over multiple frames. gfxCacheIdxB ($064A) controls the frame delay between brightness steps — higher values produce a slower fade. Each step writes the current brightness to INIDISP.

- Type 1 (Instant blank): Single call to UpdateFrameDialogue, then sets INIDISP to 0. Fastest transition.

- Type 2 (Mosaic dissolve): Brightness ramps down from $0F to 0 while MOSAIC register increases (pixel size grows). The mosaic value is computed as (15 − brightness) << 4 | 3, creating a dissolve effect as the screen fades.

- Type 3 (Wave scroll): Initializes the HDMA sine wave ($0070 = spatial frequency 6, $006E = amplitude 0, if not already running). Clamps the speed byte B (gfxCacheIdxB) to 8. Stage 1 runs 128 − 16×B frames, raising the amplitude by 1 per frame. Stage 2 steps brightness $0F → 0, holding each level for B frames while the amplitude keeps rising each frame, so the distortion keeps growing as the screen fades out. Each frame runs ApplyScrollWaveEffect.

- Type 4 (Wave alternate): Jumps to ScreenExitTransition_WaveAlt for a variant wave pattern.

All types (except instant) call UpdateFrameDialogue each frame to keep audio and display sync running during the transition.
ScreenExitTransition_WaveAlt:
Alternative wave exit transition — variant loop structure.

Similar to type 3 but with a different nesting pattern: the wave iteration count per brightness level is controlled by gfxCacheIdxB directly (rather than being computed from it). Brightness starts at $0F and decrements each outer iteration. Each inner iteration raises the wave amplitude ($006E) by 1, runs ApplyScrollWaveEffect (which syncs one frame) and then calls UpdateFrameDialogue again, so a pass takes two frames.

Initializes the HDMA sine wave system ($0070 = frequency 6, $006E = amplitude 0) if not already running. Clears both on completion.
ScrollDialogueUp:
Scroll the dialogue box content up by one tile row (8 pixels).

Starting at the content origin ($099A), copies the tile row $40 bytes below into each row, 2w tiles wide, for 2h rows (the counter 2h−1 runs one extra pass because of the BPL loop). The last copy takes its source from the extra blank row below the text area, which therefore leaves the final row blank. Sets displayModeFlags bit 0 when done. Called twice by DialogCmd_NewLine (with a WaitOneFrame after each call) to move one full text line (two tile rows).
SelectFormation: Picks the formation layout for the companions counted by ScanPartyArray: the pointer comes from companion_formation_tables (entry N for N companions) and is kept in $18 / $1A for the dot spawn loop; the leader's animation index (party array word 0) goes to actor $28.
SetPlayerTransition:
Set the player actor's function pointer and clear its frame timer.

Stores A into $0000,Y (function pointer low word) and zeros $0008,Y (frame wait counter) for immediate execution on the next actor tick. Y must point to the player actor slot. Used by melody handlers and UseItem_Aura to override the player's behavior state.
SetupHdmaChannel_Direct:
Bind the next free HDMA channel in direct mode. Same entry convention as SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect (A = bank | register << 8, Y = table address) but DMAP gets the plain hdma_channel_config mode.

The shared tail (loc_03E186, also reached from the indirect entry) pops the register number into BBADx, stores Y into A1Tx and the bank into A1Bx, sets this channel's bit ($68) in the HDMA enable mask ($66), shifts $68 left and adds $10 to $6A. There is no CLC before that ADC: the carry is the carry-out of ASL $0068, clear for channels 1–6, so at most seven channels (1–7) can be bound per frame.

Direct HDMA: each table entry is a line count followed by the register value(s) to write.
SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect:
Bind the next free HDMA channel in indirect mode (JSL from the HDMA COP handlers and the thinker scripts).

Entry: 16-bit A = table bank (low byte) | PPU B-bus register number (high byte, e.g. $0D = BG1HOFS), Y = HDMA table address. The routine pushes the bank, then the register number, uses the register number to index hdma_channel_config (DMAP transfer mode), ORs $40 (indirect) into it and writes DMAP of the channel whose register block offset is in $6A. The bank also goes to DASB (indirect data bank), so the table and the data it points to share one bank. It then branches into the shared tail inside SetupHdmaChannel_Direct (loc_03E186).

Indirect HDMA: each table entry is a line count plus a pointer to the data, so the data can live elsewhere in the bank and be changed per frame without rewriting the table.
SkipToSceneTransition: Start pressed during the end-of-route countdown: restore the deferred sceneNext/$0652, clear the state block and yield; the scene changes at once without the dive.
SortActors_BuildFinalList:
Build the final depth-sorted actor list from the bucket sort buffer.

Phase 1 — Bucket insertion: Sets SP to $0BFF to iterate the $0C00 sort buffer via PLX/PLA. For each entry, uses the sort key as an index into the $0200–$03FE bucket array. Each bucket holds a linked list of 4-byte nodes (actor slot word + next pointer word) allocated from a sequential pool starting at $0422.

Phase 2 — Linearization: Sets SP to $01FF to iterate the bucket array front-to-back via PLY. Empty buckets (zero) are skipped. Each non-empty bucket's linked list is traversed and the actor slot IDs are written sequentially to $0C00,X, producing the final render-order list. Terminated with STZ. Each chain is walked newest-node-first, so actors that share a key come out in reverse list order. After copying a chain, a PHA/PLA pair writes the zero end-of-chain word back over the bucket word just popped, which re-zeroes the bucket for the next frame's sort.

Restores original SP, DP, and processor state before returning via RTL.
SortActors_OffScreen:
Mark an actor as off-screen during depth sort processing.

Sets bit 14 ($4000) in the actor's primary flags ($10) via TSB, then continues to the next actor in the linked list via $04.
SortActorsByDepth:
Depth-sort all on-screen actors into the render list at $0C00 using bucket sort.

Iterates the actor linked list ($0058 head → $04 next). For each actor, performs screen-bounds culling on both axes (X range 0–$100 against bg1ScrollH, Y range 0–$E0 against mapScrollV), using the actor's left/right extents ($18/$1C, from the sign-extended X offset pair) and top/bottom extents ($1A/$1E, from the Y pair) that UpdateActorAnimation loads from the frame header. Off-screen actors get flag $4000 set in $10 via SortActors_OffScreen.

On-screen actors receive a depth sort key based on flags ($10):
- Bit 13 ($2000): hidden — skipped, no buffer entry
- Bits 0-1 ($0003) both clear: Y-based key = (screenY EOR $FF) ASL → actors lower on screen get lower keys and OAM indexes, so they draw in front of actors higher up
- Bit 0 only (COP SetPriorityMin): key $01FE → last in the list, behind every Y-sorted actor
- Bit 1 (COP SetPriorityMax): key $00FF EOR $FF ASL = $0000 → first in the list, in front of everything (also the result for a screen Y of $100 or more, which includes negative values)

Actor slot IDs and sort keys are written as 4-byte pairs to $0C00,Y. After all actors are processed, falls through to SortActors_BuildFinalList.
SpawnDotLoop: Dot spawn loop: one CompanionDotMovement per non-empty slot $0D62-$0D6A. Each gets its animation index, its slot pair from the layout, and the leader's pair as home.
SpawnSceneActors:
Spawn all actors defined in the current scene's actor definition table.

Clears the actor linked list head ($56) and tail ($58). Reads the scene_actors table using sceneTableIndex ($0646 = sceneCurrent × 2) to find the scene's actor definition data.

For each actor entry in the table (terminated by $FF byte):
1. Allocates a slot via actor_pool.ActorPoolAllocator (the pool-full result Y = $1FC0 is not checked)
2. Links the new slot into a doubly-linked list ($04=prev, $06=next)
3. Calls InitActorFromSceneData to parse the binary actor record
4. Carry from InitActorFromSceneData: clear = actor created, loop continues; set = the LAST record was an already-defeated enemy (AdvanceSceneDataAndFree returned its slot and unlinked it), so the loop ends. A defeated enemy followed by more records never returns here: its slot is re-used for the next record inside AdvanceSceneDataAndFree

The last live actor becomes the list tail ($58). After all actors are spawned, sets playerActorDp ($09F4) to $1000 (first actor slot; the player is expected to be the first record — inferred).
SpawnSceneThinkers:
Spawn scene-specific thinker actors from the scene_thinkers table.

Looks up the thinker list pointer from scene_thinkers[$0646]. If zero, the scene has no thinkers. Otherwise, reads thinker records in a loop:

1. Allocates a thinker slot via ThinkerPoolAlloc
2. Links into a doubly-linked list ($0004 = prev, $0006 = next)
3. Calls InitThinkerFromSceneData to parse the record
4. Terminates when data byte = $FF

Stores list head at $005A and tail at $005C. Uses bank $008C for thinker data.
SpcFadeOutHandshake:
Entry of the FadeThenStartMusic thinker: request the SPC engine's fade-out, then hand over to SpcTransferMusicData.

1. Sends $F1 to APUIO0 (the engine's CmdFadeOut: fade counters $30/$31 = $FF) and yields one frame. If APUIO0 does not echo $F1 the routine returns and runs again next frame.
2. With the echo seen, sends $01 and yields again. If APUIO0 now reads zero, execution falls into SpcTransferMusicData; otherwise it returns and retries.

Runs as a thinker script: each COP SetEntryHereAndYield suspends it until the next frame, so the handshake costs a few frames but never blocks the main loop. Not traced: whether the fade is audible before SpcTransferMusicData's $F0 stop arrives one or two frames later.
SpcTransferMusicData:
Thinker script that requests the music upload and waits for the main loop to perform it (entry of StartMusic's thinker; also reached from SpcFadeOutHandshake).

Sends $F0 (the engine's CmdStop), yields and requires a zero echo; yields again, sends $FF (jump into the engine's resident IPL-clone loader, which then posts $BBAA) and copies the music ID from chatPtr into musicTransitionState ($06FA); this staged ID is what LoadMusicFromTransitionState picks up.

Then waits (one yield per frame) for musicTransitionState = $FFFF, which LoadMusicFromTransitionState writes after the blocking SpcBlockTransfer. Once seen: COP WaitByte #01 (a two-tick delay, N + 1; not an SPC acknowledgment), sends $01, yields once more, clears sfxQueueCh1 and musicTransitionState and ends with COP Die.

Only the block transfer itself blocks the main loop; every protocol step here is spread over frames.
split_bgmode_template: BGMODE template: 7F 07 | 18 07 | 01 09 | 00 (line count, value pairs; the final byte is never copied).
split_coldata_template: COLDATA template: 7F 00 | 18 00 | 01 FF | 00 (line count, value pairs; the final byte is never copied).
SplitOpeningSequence: Opening sequence: 2 frames of rebuild + queue, 40 frames of offset += 2, then the parked final state.
ThinkerPoolAlloc:
Allocate one thinker slot from the free list pool.

Reads the next free slot address via indirect long load [$52]. If the value is negative ($FFFF sentinel), the pool is exhausted — returns with carry set (failure). Otherwise, zeroes the consumed entry to prevent double-allocation, advances the pool pointer ($52) by 2 bytes, transfers the allocated slot address to Y, and returns with carry clear (success).

Called by SpawnThinker and SpawnThinkerParam COP handlers.
TileCollision_BlockH:
Handle horizontal collision blocking — snap actor position to tile boundary.

Restores DP from actor slot (TXA/TCD). Sets solid-contact flag ($0004) in actor flags $10 via TSB.

Two snap paths based on movement direction ($001A sign):

Positive (rightward): computes (position + hitboxOffset + delta), AND $FFF0 to snap to the left edge of the blocking tile. Subtracts hitbox offset for final actor X.

Negative (leftward): same computation but rounds up — if not already tile-aligned (BIT $000F), applies AND $FFF0 + $0010 to snap to the next tile boundary (right edge of blocking tile). Subtracts hitbox offset.

Both paths PLA/PLB to discard the stacked pixel position and restore DBR, then return with carry set (blocked).
TileCollision_BlockV:
Handle vertical collision blocking — snap actor Y position to tile boundary.

Same algorithm as TileCollision_BlockH but operates on the Y axis: uses $001E (Y delta), $0001,Y (Y hitbox offset), and writes final position to $16.

Positive (downward): AND $FFF0 snap to top edge of blocking tile.
Negative (upward): AND $FFF0 + $0010 round-up snap.

Returns with carry set (blocked).
TileCollision_CheckAdjacentH:
Sub-tile boundary check for horizontal type-0 tiles.

Reads the stacked pixel Y ($01,S, pushed by MoveLeft/MoveRight) and tests the low 4 bits. If exactly on a tile boundary (bits = 0), passes through — the actor's edge covers only the scanned rows.

If misaligned, the edge also overlaps one more row: AdvanceTileOffsetY (+Y, one tile down) and test that byte via [$80],Y. If it is zero (empty), passes. If nonzero, jumps to BlockH.
TileCollision_CheckAdjacentV:
Sub-tile boundary check for vertical type-0 tiles.

Same logic as TileCollision_CheckAdjacentH but for vertical movement: tests low 4 bits of the stacked pixel X (pushed by MoveUp/MoveDown). If misaligned, also checks the tile to the right (+X, AdvanceTileOffsetX). Nonzero → BlockV, zero → pass.
TileCollision_MoveDown:
Check downward tile collision along the actor's bottom hitbox edge.

Same structure as TileCollision_MoveUp with bottom-edge adjustments: DEC before >>4 to get the correct tile row, then adds hitbox height ($0003,Y) to the tile Y coordinate for the bottommost row.

Otherwise identical horizontal scan loop and vertical tile type dispatch.
TileCollision_MoveLeft:
Check leftward tile collision along the actor's left hitbox edge.

Saves DBR and sets DP to page zero for scratch access. Computes trial X = delta + position ($18). Calls CheckActorOnSpecialTile; if on special tile, aborts immediately (restore DBR, return).

Switches DBR to the actor's sprite-data bank ($7F0008,X, the bank byte next to spritesetPtr, via PHA/PLB) so that $0000,Y reads the hitbox header; the collision map itself is read through the long pointer [$80]. Reads hitbox from metasprite header: height ($0003,Y) = vertical tile span, X offset ($0000,Y) = left edge (always negative, see header). Computes left-edge pixel X and validates against camera bounds; out-of-bounds positions are treated as type $0F (unconditional solid).

Converts pixel coordinates to tile indices (>>4) and calls CalcTileMapOffset. Scans down the leading edge (+Y, via AdvanceTileOffsetY) through $0E tiles: for each, reads the collision byte via [$80],Y. High nibble ($F0) nonzero = immediate solid → BlockH. Low nibble = tile type; type 0 with rows remaining → advance and continue. Otherwise (a nonzero type, or type 0 on the last row) dispatch through TileTypeJumpTable_Horizontal; type 0 then lands in CheckAdjacentH, which looks one row further when the actor is not tile-aligned in Y.

The PHA before the Y-to-tile conversion pushes the raw pixel Y for use by CheckAdjacentH's sub-tile alignment test.
TileCollision_MoveRight:
Check rightward tile collision along the actor's right hitbox edge.

Same structure as TileCollision_MoveLeft with two differences:
1. Right edge X = left offset + trial X − 1 (DEC for inclusive edge), plus hitbox width ($0002,Y) added to the tile column after conversion
2. Camera bounds check adds +$0010 (one tile width) then subtracts back, ensuring the full 16-pixel right edge fits within bounds

Otherwise identical vertical scan loop and tile type dispatch.
TileCollision_MoveUp:
Check upward tile collision along the actor's top hitbox edge.

Same structure as TileCollision_MoveLeft but for vertical movement. Uses hitbox width ($0002,Y) as the horizontal tile span to scan, and Y offset ($0001,Y) for the top edge. Computes X from $0000,Y + actor X.

Scans along the top edge (+X, via AdvanceTileOffsetX) through $0E tiles. Out-of-bounds Y positions are treated as type $0F (solid).
TileCollision_PassH: No horizontal collision — restore DP from actor slot, discard stacked pixel position (PLA), restore DBR (PLB), return with carry clear.
TileCollision_PassV: No vertical collision — restore DP, discard stacked pixel position, restore DBR, return carry clear.
TileCollision_SolidH: Unconditional horizontal solid — TYX restores X = actor slot (Y held it since the jump-table dispatch) and falls through to TileCollision_BlockH.
TileCollision_SolidV: Unconditional vertical solid — TYX restores X = actor slot (Y held it since the jump-table dispatch) and jumps to TileCollision_BlockV.
TileTypeJumpTable_Horizontal:
16-entry jump table for horizontal tile type dispatch.

Indexed by (tile_type × 2) from the low nibble of the collision byte. Entry 0 = TileCollision_CheckAdjacentH (sub-tile boundary test). Entries 1–F all point to TileCollision_SolidH (unconditional solid).
TileTypeJumpTable_Vertical:
16-entry jump table for vertical tile type dispatch.

Indexed by (tile_type × 2). Entry 0 = TileCollision_CheckAdjacentV, entries 1–F = TileCollision_SolidV.
TiltPhaseStart: Tilt phase. Looks up and shows the name of the scene being left ($0D6F), then 93 ticks of gravity-curve growth in $B6 (perspective) and $B8 + 1.
UpdateActorAnimation:
Advance an actor's animation frame and update metasprite/bounding box pointers.

Switches DBR to the actor's sprite bank ($7F0008,X). Indexes into the spriteset table at entry $28 (animation set), then indexes frame $2A within that animation (×4 for 4-byte frame entries).

If the frame data word is negative (BMI), the animation has ended: resets $2A to 0 and returns with carry SET to signal the caller.

Otherwise, updates the metasprite pointer ($7F000C,X) to the frame's sprite data (+ 4 for the sub-sprite array). Reads X/Y bounding box offset pairs from the frame header, sign-extending bytes via $0080 check and ORA $FF00. The mirror bits of $0E (ROL moves bit 15 into carry and bit 14 into N) swap the byte order of each offset pair via XBA: V-flip for the Y pair, H-flip for the X pair.

Stores the X pair as signed extents $18 (left) / $1C (right) and the Y pair as unsigned extents $1A (top) / $1E (bottom) — the values SortActorsByDepth uses for culling — and conditionally updates the collision box ($20 = X pair, $22 = Y pair) based on $12 flags:
- Bit 8 ($0100): skip collision box update entirely
- Bit 7 ($0080): copy raw offsets to $20/$22 (no ×8 centering adjustment)
- Neither: apply -8px centering to $22 before storing

Increments frame counter $2A. Returns with carry CLEAR on success.
UseItem_Apple: Apple — consumable healing item. Removes from inventory and sets hpToHeal to 1, triggering a brief HP restoration effect. Unlike Herb, no confirmation dialogue.
UseItem_Aura:
Aura — Shadow's transformation ability.

Multiple guard conditions must pass: playerFlags bits $1000 (on a slope) and $0100 (forced walk) must be clear, both playerSpeedEw and playerSpeedNs must be zero (standing still), and characterForm must be 2 (Shadow). On success, overwrites the player actor's function pointer to PlayerAuraTransformEntry via SetPlayerTransition, initiating the Aura transformation sequence. If not Shadow or any guard fails, prints failure message or returns silently.
UseItem_CrystalBall:
Crystal Ball — place in pedestals in Mu (scene $4C).

Four placement positions, each with an independent flag ($60–$63). All four use the same placement message. If a ball is already placed, prints a duplicate message. Unlike most key items, the Crystal Ball is removed via RemoveEquippedItem (JSR) rather than COP RemoveItem, since the same item can be placed in multiple slots.
UseItem_DiamondBlock:
Diamond Block — fit into a tile slot in the Diamond Mine (scene $25).

Checks tiles ($0E–$0F, $19–$1A). Falls through to UseItem_DiamondBlock_Place on match.
UseItem_DiamondBlock_Place: Diamond Block placement — removes item and sets flag $2F.
UseItem_ElevatorKey:
Elevator Key — activate the mine elevator (scene $3F).

Checks tiles ($18,$34)–($1A,$37). Removes item and sets flag $69.
UseItem_FatherJournal: Father's Journal — display-only. Shows the hieroglyph decipherment text.
UseItem_FluteConfigureController: After a successful SpawnListAppend of FluteMusicActorController from UseItem_WindMelody (Y holds the new slot): ORs display-filter bit $1000 into the controller $12, sets track $19 in $26 and melody index 0 in $20, restores X, returns to the caller.
UseItem_GorgonFlower:
Gorgon Flower — place petals in three statue mouths (scene $AE).

Three positions, each gated by an independent flag: ($06,$06)–($07,$08) flag $BF, ($08,$06)–($09,$08) flag $C0, ($0A,$06)–($0B,$08) flag $C1. After placing each petal, checks whether all three flags are set. Only when all three are placed is the item removed from inventory via COP RemoveItem. This partial-use mechanic is unique among IOG items.
UseItem_Herb:
Herb — healing item with yes/no confirmation.

Scene $CD (Tower of Babel) only. If flag $0F is set (Memory Melody already played), shows a timing message. Otherwise checks tile region ($04,$09)–($0C,$0B) for the puzzle area, then presents a 6-option dialogue (code_039AC2) to choose a slot position.

After selection, the loc_039B0F subroutine extracts the plate ID (item byte − $1E, stored in $0AA6), removes the plate from inventory, and spawns a metatile-drawing actor. If the chosen slot ($0B28 table, indexed by $0AAC) already contains a plate, the old plate is returned to inventory via GiveItemToPlayer before the new one is stored. Empty slots ($FFFF) receive a first-time placement message.

Checks tiles ($26–$27, $15–$16), the mantel statue B belongs on. Otherwise, if flag $44 is set it prints the spirits hint; if not it prints a generic query about the Inca secret. Alternate position check for Inca Statue B. Same logic as UseItem_IncaStatueA_CheckAlt but with swapped mantel positions.

Outside scene $24, prints 'nothing happened.' If not Will, prints 'doesn't have the Flute.'

WaitNFrames_Entry: Wait for A frames. Saves processor state (PHP), switches to 8-bit A (SEP #$20), and branches to the wait loop body. If worldReadyFlag is zero, returns immediately without waiting (game not yet in rendering state).
WaitNFrames_Loop: Counts A down, calling UpdateFrameDialogue once per frame (the lightweight tick: audio and display, no game logic).
WaitNFrames_PerChar:
Wait for the per-character frame delay stored in $007E.

Saves processor state, switches to 8-bit. If $007E = 0, returns immediately (instant text mode). Otherwise falls into the wait loop. Each iteration calls UpdateFrameDialogue to process a lightweight frame update (audio, display sync) without advancing game logic.
WaitOneFrame: Wait exactly one frame by loading A = 1 and falling through to WaitNFrames_Entry.

With no choice id (scripted trip) it dies at once and the child does all the work.
